codes.name: EXTINCTION_CONDITIONS_PARTIAL
codes.condition: Fires on an extinction class whose printed reflection conditions do not name every absence the class implies (`not cand.conditions_complete`, indexing/diagnostics.py:1015).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Arithmetic on the class's own absence set against its readable summary; the screen used the full set, so no score, rank or pick moves. The info level says nothing is owed for any purpose, which matches what it reports.

codes.name: EXTINCTION_FORBIDDEN_INTENSITY
codes.condition: Fires on a class refuted because at least one testable forbidden position carries net intensity of ABSENT_SIGMA (3) times its propagated sigma or more against the class's own Pawley y_calc (indexing/extinction.py:1524-1545; diagnostics.py:992).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); WP-1077 sham probes; no second or third family named for the firing side.
codes.evidence: The testability rule (`_model_is_quiet`, WP-1077) and the absence test against the class's own fit are rietx's own; ABSENT_SIGMA's 3 is the 99.7 % window shared with MATCH_SIGMA, and one present position suffices to refute. **Demotes a candidate:** `refuted=True` sorts the class below every unrefuted one (extinction.py:1568) and `best_or_none` cannot return it. Unanimity: no; a careful refiner who reads the excess as an impurity line at a forbidden position keeps the class (the code's own suggestion says so), and the gallery's zincite row records its true 6_3 screw and c-glide still refuted (tests/indexing_gallery.py, zincite).
codes.question: A single 3-sigma position refutes and demotes a class, and the true zincite class is refuted on disk; should a refuted class keep its ranked place with its present-position count as the evidence (report), rather than be sorted below every unrefuted class (refuse)?

codes.name: EXTINCTION_GROUPS_NOT_SEPARABLE
codes.condition: Fires when the leading extinction class admits more than one space group (`len(top.space_groups) > 1`, indexing/diagnostics.py:1129).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Group theory: members of one extinction symbol differ only by elements that produce no systematic absence, so the statement is physics and fires whenever it is true. Info is the right level, since no data could act on it; the full list travels and no group is picked.

codes.name: EXTINCTION_PRIOR_APPLIED
codes.condition: Fires when a declared ExtinctionPrior (Sohncke, centrosymmetric, polar, Z or density) removed space groups from some classes, at warning when it emptied the data's leading class or a declared density contradicts Z, at info otherwise (indexing/diagnostics.py:1272, `_prior_diagnostic`).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: The filter is opt-in (`determine_extinction_symbol(restrict=)`, off by default) and moves no Delta-BIC; membership is group theory and the density test uses DENSITY_Z_TOLERANCE (1.5 %, International Tables Vol. C ch. 3.2, tier 2 on its row, WP-2033). The level split (warning when the declaration and the data disagree) is the caller-visible half of best_or_none's abstention and reads two different consequences, so it is not a threshold between levels. The withdrawn INDEX_Z_NOT_INTEGER (schemas/indexing.py:218, WP-2030) is not this code: its volume-window rule is WP-2030's to own (WP-1510 entry).
codes.question: WP-2033's inherited entry: the `z_candidates` field comment on ExtinctionScreen (schemas/indexing.py ~2547) still says two whole Z fit from Z of about 50, where the 1.5 % tolerance gives two from Z of about 33 (extinction.py:184 already says 33); correct it when DENSITY_Z_TOLERANCE's row is written?

codes.name: EXTINCTION_SCREEN_FAILED
codes.condition: Fires at error when the prefit or reference fit raised, or when the lattice group predicts no reflection in the measured range (indexing/extinction.py:1302, :1347).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: A raised fit or an empty reflection set is arithmetic, and no class is scored, so there is nothing to read; error is the rule's level for that. It removes no cell and picks nothing, and REFERENCE_NET_RWP_MAX is read first so a reference that models nothing reports as unreliable instead (extinction.py:1336-1340, WP-2076).

codes.name: EXTINCTION_SCREEN_UNRELIABLE
codes.condition: Fires when the absence-free reference fit's background-subtracted Rwp exceeds REFERENCE_NET_RWP_MAX (0.7071) or is unmeasured (indexing/diagnostics.py:1069; extinction.py:1336).
codes.measured_on: Already tiered: silent side on four real families, firing side on synthetic Si, SRM 676a at x1.02 and GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab) at x0.99 (_audit.py:678).
codes.evidence: Already tiered (tier 3, approved 2026-10-21, PR #939): the row's tier is copied into threshold and action. The statistic is Toby's (2006, Powder Diffr. 21, 67) background-subtracted Rwp, as REFERENCE_NET_RWP_MAX's comment cites. The action withholds the pick and keeps the ranking.

codes.name: EXTINCTION_SYMBOL_AMBIGUOUS
codes.condition: Fires at warning when the runner-up class lies within DECISIVE_DELTA_BIC (10) of the leader, a declared prior is contradicted, the leader has no testable absence, classes were left unfitted or raised, every class was refuted, or the screen was cancelled or had no candidates; at info on a class with no testable absence (indexing/diagnostics.py:1003, :1093, :1101, :1179).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (SRM 676a corundum); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II PbSO4 X-ray (Hill 1992); synthetic P2_1/c (tests/test_extinction_gate.py, test_extinction_margin.py).
codes.evidence: The statistic is Schwarz's BIC difference with the penalty counted on testable lines only (WP-2076); the threshold is Kass & Raftery (1995, J. Am. Stat. Assoc. 90, 773) 'very strong', as extinction.py:149 cites. The action withholds `best_or_none` and keeps the full ranking, which is DESIGN.md Rule 1's second-kind posture; it removes no class. Unanimity: yes, none found, since a caller who would accept 'strong' evidence (6-10) still has every class's Delta-BIC in the ranking.
codes.question: The GUI route calls `screen.best_or_none()` (gui/session.py:2803), so the pick under this margin sits on a default path; is DECISIVE_DELTA_BIC therefore the unanimity margin the WP's best_or_none task tiers (tier 2 by Kass & Raftery)?

codes.name: INDEX_ABSTAINED
codes.condition: Fires whenever `IndexingResult.best_or_none()` returns None: no candidate, or not exactly one candidate graded high without ambiguity partners; warning with candidates, error with none (indexing/diagnostics.py:893-912).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: The statistic is arithmetic over the gate's grades (schemas/indexing.py:2245-2263). The threshold is the gate itself: high needs zero caveats and every engine behind the cell (consensus.py:765-769), with INDEX_REFUTING_CAVEATS's split rietx's own (WP-1024, WP-1042). The action withholds the pick and keeps the ranking with every caveat. Unanimity on withholding: yes, none found; on the level: on real data with no measured shift `high` is unreachable by design (shift_allowance_assumed, indexing/CLAUDE.md), so this warning fires on nearly every default run.
codes.question: Attention clause 1: a warning that fires on nearly every real-data run tells no fit from another; should the abstention be the record (best_or_none None plus the caveats) and the code fire only where it says something a run can differ on? And is error right for an empty search, which is an answer rather than unreadable values? Separately, best_or_none is reached on default paths: workflow._emit_end's `index_end` event carries its cell (workflow.py:1211), the CLI exit code (cli.py:374) and the GUI's picked row (gui/session.py:2593).

codes.name: INDEX_BRAVAIS_AMBIGUOUS

guards: cand.bravais is not None and (cand.bravais.ambiguous or cand.bravais.methods_disagree)

codes.condition: Fires when the lattice reads a higher symmetry only at a loose tolerance in the sweep (BRAVAIS_OBLIQUITIES 0.5-3 deg for gemmi, BRAVAIS_SYMPREC_SIGMAS 1, 3, 10 x the cell esd for spglib) or the two tools disagree at their tightest (indexing/diagnostics.py:751).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: The statistic is Le Page's (1982) obliquity via gemmi plus spglib's symprec (reduce.py:5, :117-123); the sweep values are rietx's. The act is the capping caveat `bravais_ambiguous` (consensus.py:723) and the lower system reported; nothing is refuted or removed. Unanimity on reporting the lower symmetry and capping high: yes, none found. A candidate with `bravais is None` gets the caveat with no diagnostic.

codes.name: INDEX_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED
codes.condition: Fires when the whole-run ceiling's clock, not a user cancel, stopped the run, naming engines not run, systems truncated or not reached, and candidates not validated (indexing/engines.py:2314).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) corundum (121.3 s) and GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab) (130.7 s), WP-1986 entry; the quick preset's 120 s from WP-1042 on darwin arm64.
codes.evidence: The fact is arithmetic. The default threshold is the quick preset's QUICK_TOTAL_BUDGET_SECONDS (120 s, engines.py:2345), rietx's own and not answer-invariant (WP task 2); a declared total_budget_seconds is the caller's. The act truncates trailing systems: unvalidated candidates read `not_validated` (capping), unreached candidates read `geometric_ambiguity` (refuting) and grade low. Unanimity on a bounded first search: no, a caller after a low-symmetry cell the ceiling cuts is a dissenter (the WP's own case against).
codes.question: #1374's share rule: one (engine x system) unit can hold the whole declared ceiling, so a single slow unit can leave every later system unreached; should a unit's share be bounded? And the unreached-candidate refutation above is the same capping-vs-refuting question as INDEX_GEOMETRIC_AMBIGUITY's.

codes.name: INDEX_CANDIDATES_TRUNCATED
codes.condition: Fires when consensus merged more distinct lattices than max_candidates (DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES 12) or a unit returned a full engine pool (indexing/engines.py:2261).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: The merge clause is an exact count of what lies outside the list; the pool clause is a flag that cannot count. Under the listing-cap rule (tier 1 once a test shows the report complete inside the cap and its notes count what lies outside) only the merge clause qualifies. The cut lattices are never validated or graded, so the cap also bounds what the answer can contain. Unanimity: yes, none found, while the count is stated.
codes.question: Is DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES a listing cap (tier 1, given a completeness test) or a cap on the answer (tier 3), given that the pool clause names units without a count?

codes.name: INDEX_CELL_SYSTEMATIC_UNQUANTIFIED
codes.condition: Fires on every run with candidates when no instrument was supplied or the geometry is Bragg-Brentano, stating BRAGG_BRENTANO_CELL_PPM (85 ppm) as the unquantified systematic (indexing/diagnostics.py:950, :963).
codes.measured_on: One study (tag guillemot-study, audit_tools.py check A): one lab Bragg-Brentano family.
codes.evidence: The 85 ppm is rietx's own measurement (goniometer radius swept 180-320 mm moves Rwp 0.029 points while about 85 ppm lands on the cell); it is the meaning of the cell esd, not a verdict, and it moves nothing. Info is right for the level, but the code fires on every Bragg-Brentano run with candidates.
codes.question: Attention clause 1: a diagnostic firing on every Bragg-Brentano run tells no run from another; should it become a record field on the result (the cell's unquantified systematic, keyed in rietx.help) with one report line?

codes.name: INDEX_DATA_INSUFFICIENT
codes.condition: Fires at error, and no engine runs, when the list has fewer than two usable lines, fewer than MIN_LINES_PER_DOF (5) usable lines per metric degree of freedom in every system, or a median sigma(Q)/Q above MAX_RELATIVE_SIGMA_Q (1e-3) on a fitted list (indexing/quality.py:426-491; workflow.py:962-975; engines' own two-line guards at dichotomy.py:807, svd.py:668, trial_error.py:289).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); bethanechol positions (the sigma arm is skipped on positions).
codes.evidence: **A gate that still refuses:** `supports_indexing=False` returns an empty result before any engine runs (workflow.py:962). The two-line arm is arithmetic (kind 1). The other two thresholds are rietx's: MIN_LINES_PER_DOF 'is not a statistical threshold' (schemas/indexing.py:470) and MAX_RELATIVE_SIGMA_Q is a resolving-power scale argument after Mighell & Santoro (1975), not a tested value. Unanimity: no; WP-1043 already moved the 20-line bar from refusing to reporting after fluorite's 18 clean cubic lines were refused, and an engine run with a widened tolerance on imprecise lines is ordinary practice.
codes.question: Should the per-DOF and sigma(Q)/Q arms report (search anyway, grade every candidate with a refuting or capping caveat naming the number) rather than refuse, keeping refusal for the two-line arithmetic case only, per 'gates report evidence, never refuse'?

codes.name: INDEX_DOMINANT_ZONE
codes.condition: Fires when the merged harvest was empty and the trial_error probe found a cell in a system with at most DOMINANT_ZONE_MAX_DOF (2) metric degrees of freedom only at a wider index table (DOMINANT_ZONE_PROBE_LADDER 3, 5, 9; DOMINANT_ZONE_PROBE_SECONDS 30 s per rung) (indexing/trial_error.py:567).
codes.measured_on: One synthetic construction (tetragonal, c = 26 A); no real family.
codes.evidence: The statistic is measured, not inferred (a census statistic failed, WP-1019). BASE_INDEX_MAX 2 and the ladder are rietx's. The act is a warning only: the cells the probe found are not returned as candidates.
codes.question: The probe finds cells and discards them, reporting only that they exist; should the found cells be returned in the ranking with their wider-index provenance, per 'report evidence, never refuse'?

codes.name: INDEX_GEOMETRIC_AMBIGUITY
codes.condition: Fires on a candidate with ambiguity partners: derivative lattices up to MAX_AMBIGUITY_INDEX (4) whose mean |dQ| is within AMBIGUITY_DISCREPANCY_SLACK (1.5) of the parent's and that the in-range absence test does not refute (indexing/diagnostics.py:730; ambiguity.py).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer) (half-volume rival); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a).
codes.evidence: The statistic is Mighell & Santoro's (1975) derivative-lattice ambiguity; the index fence and the 1.5 slack are rietx's (ambiguity.py:88, :99). **Demotes a candidate:** `geometric_ambiguity` is in INDEX_REFUTING_CAVEATS, so the candidate grades low and `best_or_none` refuses it. A candidate never reached by the sweep (outside CONSENSUS_CHECK_TOP's three and not found by every engine, or stopped by the ceiling) gets the same refuting caveat (consensus.py:671-674) and this code does not fire on it, since it keys on `cand.ambiguity`. Unanimity on refuting where partners exist: yes, none found.
codes.question: WP-1986 entry: the caveat for a candidate the ambiguity search never reached (consensus.py:671, the ~627 docstring) refutes, so under a binding ceiling every unreached candidate grades low, and so does every candidate ranked below three that two of three engines found; is that 'capping' (an unasked question) or 'refuting'? WP-2013 rewrote the comments to say refuting; if the ruling is capping, the code and those words change together, and an unreached candidate should say so in its own diagnostic.

codes.name: INDEX_IMPURITY_LINES

guards: lebail is not None and lebail.unmatched_observed

codes.condition: Fires on any validated candidate whose Pawley validation leaves at least one observed peak with no calculated reflection nearby (`lebail.unmatched_observed > 0`, indexing/diagnostics.py:833).
codes.measured_on: WP-1041: 21 validated candidates on six known-cell datasets (NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab)).
codes.evidence: The count is deliberately not a caveat: WP-1041 measured it at 10-188 on correct cells, its level being the specimen's, and found it comparative only (consensus.py:652-663). The > 0 trigger is rietx's. The act is a per-candidate warning; it moves no grade or rank. Unanimity on the warning level: no, since on WP-1041's numbers it fires on the true cell of every validated dataset, including 11-BM NAC's truth with 188 unmatched against a CaF2 impurity.
codes.question: A warning that fires on correct cells by WP-1041's own measurement fails attention clause 1; should the count be a record field ranked across candidates (it is already `lebail.unmatched_observed`) with no per-candidate warning?

codes.name: INDEX_INLIER_RETRY
codes.condition: Fires when the first pass returned no lattice MIN_AGREEMENT (2) engines agree on and the run searched again under the inlier rule: at least INLIER_FRACTION (0.6) of the driven lines and the ANCHOR_LINES (5) strongest (indexing/engines.py:1329).
codes.measured_on: Not measured in the code's comments by family; the constants' rows carry the evidence (indexing C4).
codes.evidence: The trigger is arithmetic on the corroboration count. The inlier acceptance is RANSAC's shape (Fischler & Bolles 1981, as INLIER_FRACTION cites) with rietx's numbers. The act is a second search on the same ceiling; it removes nothing and can add cells. Unanimity: no; DICVOL's absolute unindexed-line count is the dissenting default (DEFAULT_N_UNINDEXED's comment), and a looser acceptance can manufacture cells, which the code mitigates by reporting n_search_unindexed per candidate.

codes.name: INDEX_MULTIPLE_SOLUTIONS
codes.condition: Fires when more than one candidate is graded high (`len(high) > 1`, indexing/diagnostics.py:881).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: Arithmetic count of high grades; `best_or_none` returns None and every candidate stays ranked. Unanimity: yes, none found; no refiner names one of two cells that each pass the whole gate. The action is withholding a pick, never removing a candidate.

codes.name: INDEX_NOT_VALIDATED
codes.condition: Fires when no pattern was supplied, so no candidate had a whole-profile fit (`not result.validated`, indexing/diagnostics.py:914).
codes.measured_on: hl2 bare position list (unknown phase); the bethanechol benchmark sets (positions only).
codes.evidence: The fact is arithmetic; the act is the capping caveat `not_validated` on every candidate (consensus.py:684), so high is out of reach and nothing is refuted. Capping is rietx's gate (WP-1024). Unanimity: a dissenter exists, since de Wolff (1968) reads M20 >= 10 as sufficient for a correct cell from positions alone, and the classical programs report peaks-only solutions; the cap only withholds high and leaves medium.
codes.question: Is capping a peaks-only answer at medium unanimous, given that de Wolff's M20 criterion is the field's own peaks-only acceptance (tier 2 practice)?

codes.name: INDEX_PANEL_REDUCED
codes.condition: Fires when the search is supported but the list has fewer than PEAK_MIN_USABLE_LINES (20) usable lines, so some classical figures of merit are undefined (indexing/diagnostics.py:622).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (fluorite, 18 lines).
codes.evidence: The threshold is de Wolff's (1968) M20, defined on the first twenty lines, and Smith's (1977) envelope at N = 20 (schemas/indexing.py PEAK_MIN_USABLE_LINES comment); Smith & Snyder recommend N = 30 for F_N, so scoring F_N at 20 is rietx's. The act is the capping caveat `fom_panel_reduced` (consensus.py:682), which keeps high out of reach and refutes nothing; the search still runs (WP-1043). Unanimity on capping high: yes, none found, since the panel that would score the cell is incomplete.
codes.question: PEAK_LIST_TOO_SHORT states the same fact one layer down at the same threshold; is one code enough (attention clause 1)?

codes.name: INDEX_PREDICTED_BUT_ABSENT
codes.condition: Fires when the line screen counts predicted lines no extinction could remove with nothing above the picker's envelope: warning inside de Wolff's window (first twenty lines), info outside it (indexing/diagnostics.py:790).
codes.measured_on: Already tiered: true magnetite and PbSO4 cells (count 2), NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer) wrong a-sqrt2 I cell (_audit.py:812).
codes.evidence: Already tiered (tier 3, approved 2026-10-21, C3): the row's tier is copied into statistic, threshold and action. The window is de Wolff's; the > 0 trigger is rietx's own, and the act caps the grade (`predicted_but_absent`, capping since thresholds 1.12) and ranks nothing. The level split by in-window count is two consequences (caps or caps nothing), not a threshold between levels.

codes.name: INDEX_PRIOR_USED
codes.condition: Fires when the caller declared a cell, system or space-group prior; at warning when a prior lies outside the axis box and was not checked (indexing/priors.py:379, :387).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Opt-in: priors are off by default and the code reports the requested act and each prior's fate. The box refusal is WP-1045's ruling (a prior never widens the declared search), and the warning names the SearchSpec values to pass (WP-1510).
codes.question: Condition 2 of the caller class: a prior also reorders the systems (`jumped`) and seeds an engine, which moves what a bounded run reaches; is that a package choice to tier rather than the caller's?

codes.name: INDEX_SEARCH_INCOMPLETE
codes.condition: Fires when an engine stopped before exhausting a system: its per-system budget (DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS 30 s), a grid size cap, or the run's ceiling or a cancel (indexing/engines.py:2218).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: The fact is arithmetic; the budgets and size caps are tiered on their own rows. The act is the capping caveat `search_incomplete` on every candidate of that system (consensus.py:718), so high is out of reach there. Unanimity: no, a refiner holding a cell every engine found and that validated would not discount it because the clock cut the rest of the system; the cap is defensible as 'a better cell may be missing' but is not unanimous.
codes.question: Should `search_incomplete` cap only a negative result (systems with no candidate), as its schema comment says ('a negative result elsewhere in the domain means nothing'), rather than every candidate found in that system?

codes.name: INDEX_SHIFT_ALLOWANCE
codes.condition: Fires when no shift was measured or declared and the search added an assumed allowance in quadrature to every sigma: the picked list's lower-quartile FWHM where widths were measured, else DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_SHIFT_DEG (0.05 deg) (indexing/engines.py:1311, :1264-1267).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) corundum (median 0.060 deg from the certified positions against 0.0056 deg fitted sigma).
codes.evidence: The allowance's existence is measured and its value is a policy (DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_SHIFT_DEG's comment). The act widens every matching window and adds the capping caveat `shift_allowance_assumed` (consensus.py:720), which makes high unreachable on real data with no measured shift (indexing/CLAUDE.md). Unanimity on widening: yes, none found, since every indexing program takes a matching tolerance; on capping: yes, a cell found inside an assumed window has absorbed the shift.

codes.name: INDEX_SHIFT_DETECTED

guards: shift is not None and shift.source == 'measured' and shift.best

codes.condition: Fires when a shift was measured against caller-supplied reference positions and the best template leaves the runner-up SEPARABILITY_MIN_SS_RATIO (2.0) times more residual (indexing/diagnostics.py:655; quality.py:207-216).
codes.measured_on: Not measured on a family in the code; reachable only with reference_two_theta.
codes.evidence: The templates (constant, cos theta, sin 2theta) are the textbook peak-position aberrations and the fit is weighted least squares; the 2.0 ratio is rietx's (report/schemas.py:369, unaudited on its own row). The act is a warning advising the template and the instrument correction; it does not change the search beyond the measured allowance. Unanimity on naming the cause at a 2x residual ratio: no, a careful refiner with a narrow range would not correct an instrument fault from it.

codes.name: INDEX_SHIFT_FROM_PAIRS
codes.condition: Fires when the default pair screen (shift_from_pairs=True) measured a systematic shift from harmonic reflection pairs with no reference positions (indexing/workflow.py:610-617; engines.py:1362).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer) (0.037 deg allowance recovers the certificate); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) corundum (WP-1038).
codes.evidence: The pair test (clustering against structureless replicates, WP-1038) is rietx's own. The act sets the window from the measured amplitude and lifts the `shift_allowance_assumed` cap (engines.py:1260-1263), which is what makes high reachable. Unanimity: no named dissenter for using a measured amplitude; the cause is left unnamed, as the code says.

codes.name: INDEX_SHIFT_MODEL_AMBIGUOUS

guards: shift is not None and shift.source == 'measured' and shift.best

codes.condition: Fires when a shift was measured against references and the templates are not separable at SEPARABILITY_MIN_SS_RATIO (2.0) (indexing/diagnostics.py:668).
codes.measured_on: Not measured on a family in the code; reachable only with reference_two_theta.
codes.evidence: The cause depends on the range, so the code reports the amplitude, the collinearity and the template spread and names no fault, which is DESIGN.md Rule 1's third-kind posture. The 2.0 ratio is rietx's. Warning: the spread is a systematic to carry onto every position before quoting a cell.

codes.name: INDEX_SINGLE_ENGINE
codes.condition: Fires when only one engine ran (indexing/engines.py:2279).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Opt-in: only a caller passing one engine reaches it. The act is the grade floor (fewer than MIN_AGREEMENT 2 engines grades low, consensus.py:765), which demotes every candidate by construction, and this info code says the low means unconfirmed, not refuted. MIN_AGREEMENT is rietx's corroboration rule (WP-1042, WP-1046), tiered on its row.

codes.name: INDEX_SUPERCELL_REFUTED
codes.condition: Fires when a candidate's supercell check against a higher-ranked parent reads refuted: its uncancellable extra lines are seen no more often than chance at SUPERCELL_CHANCE_ALPHA (0.01) (indexing/diagnostics.py:814).
codes.measured_on: Already tiered: acceptance corpus finished searches, brucite a x 2 supercell, APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron) P description (_audit.py:832).
codes.evidence: Already tiered (tier 3, approved 2026-11-01, PR #1302): the row's tier is copied into every part. **Demotes a candidate:** it ranks directly below its parent and `supercell_refuted` is refuting, so it grades low; it stays in the list.

codes.name: INDEX_SYSTEMS_NOT_COVERED
codes.condition: Fires when some crystal system is missing from `systems_searched` (indexing/diagnostics.py:923).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Arithmetic on the systems searched against SYSTEM_ORDER; info, and it moves no grade or rank. It names a scope the caller declared or the ceiling left.

codes.name: INDEX_VALIDATION_FAILED
codes.condition: Fires when a candidate's whole-pattern (Pawley) validation fit raised an exception (indexing/workflow.py:560).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: The fact is arithmetic. **Demotes a candidate:** the status 'failed' (and 'diverged') writes `validation_failed`, which is in INDEX_REFUTING_CAVEATS (schemas/indexing.py:703; consensus.py:686), so the candidate grades low. The code's own explanation says the candidate is 'neither supported nor refuted' (help.py:3229), and the dossier's rule one module over is 'a raised fit is no evidence' (WP-2076). Unanimity on refuting: no; the explanation itself is the dissent.
codes.question: Should a raised validation fit cap (like `not_validated`) rather than refute, matching its own explanation and WP-2076's 'a raised fit is no evidence'; and should 'diverged', which is a measurement, stay refuting as a separate caveat?

codes.name: INDEX_VOLUME_UNPHYSICAL
codes.condition: Fires on a candidate carrying `volume_unphysical`: volume below DEFAULT_MIN_VOLUME (15 A^3) or above VOLUME_ENVELOPE_SLACK (1.5) times Smith's (1977) envelope for its system (consensus.py:724-727; indexing/diagnostics.py:845).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab) (WP-1045 slack).
codes.evidence: The envelope is Smith's (1977) mean-line volume estimate; 15 A^3 and the 1.5 slack are rietx's (WP-1045). **Demotes a candidate:** `volume_unphysical` is refuting, so the cell grades low. Unanimity: yes below 15 A^3 (no lattice); no above the envelope, since Smith's estimate excludes true cells below 0.71 line-completeness by its own calibration and a caller who widened max_volume for a large cell is a named dissenter.
codes.question: Should the upper arm (above 1.5 x Smith's envelope) cap rather than refute, keeping refutation for the sub-atomic lower arm?

codes.name: LAUE_CLASS_NOT_SEPARABLE
codes.condition: Fires when the leading class's admitted groups fall in more than one Laue class (`len(top.laue_classes) > 1`, indexing/diagnostics.py:1115).
codes.measured_on: n/a
codes.evidence: Group theory: Laue classes sharing every position and absence differ only in the intensity partition inside overlapped multiplets, which a powder does not expose. Info, and it moves nothing.

codes.name: PEAK_ASYMMETRY_UNMODELLED
codes.condition: Fires on lines whose residual's odd-cubic projection exceeds PEAK_ASYMMETRY_MIN_SIGMA (4) in |t| (indexing/diagnostics.py:214).
codes.measured_on: Not measured on a named family in the constant's comment.
codes.evidence: The odd-cubic projection is rietx's statistic and 4 sigma its threshold. Reported, not removed; warning because the position, and so the cell, is pulled towards the tail.

codes.name: PEAK_AXIAL_TAIL
codes.condition: Fires on weak components within PEAK_AXIAL_TAIL_MAX_FWHM (3.5) FWHM of a stronger group-mate on the side axial divergence points (indexing/diagnostics.py:177).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer) (farthest tail 2.99 FWHM; five components carry 125 ppm of cell bias); one family.
codes.evidence: The one-sided 90-degree flip is the aberration's physics; the weak-ratio reuse and the 3.5 reach are rietx's, measured on SRM 660c only. Reported, not removed (absent from PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS): info and nothing moves.

codes.name: PEAK_CONTAMINATION_LINE
codes.condition: Fires on lines flagged `ghost_kbeta` or `ghost_tungsten` by the joint screen (several strong parents at one common ratio, GHOST_MIN_PARENTS 5, background/diagnostics.py:206) (indexing/diagnostics.py:204).
codes.measured_on: 17 bundled monochromated patterns (20 flags to none after the joint rule, WP-1442); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a).
codes.evidence: The Kbeta and W Lalpha positions are emission physics; the joint ratio rule and the GHOST_* numbers are rietx's (WP-2002 B13 proposes their tiers here). **Removes a line:** both flags are in PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS, excluded and never subtracted. Unanimity: yes for a confirmed common-ratio leak, none found.

codes.name: PEAK_EXPECTED_FALSE_LINES
codes.condition: Fires on every detected fitted list, stating the Benjamini-Hochberg bar at PEAK_FDR_Q (0.01) over the pattern's resolution elements and the expected number of noise lines kept (indexing/diagnostics.py:247).
codes.measured_on: Synthetic steep-background silicon (#728: 24 of 26 off-lattice components marked, no silicon line); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab).
codes.evidence: The statistic is Benjamini & Hochberg (1995, J. R. Stat. Soc. B 57, 289), as PEAK_FDR_Q cites; q = 0.01 is rietx's. The act: `weak_line` components stay usable but are excluded from the set that drives the search (PEAK_UNDRIVEN_FLAGS, schemas/indexing.py:872). Info, always emitted by design ('a peak list that never states its null is the defect').
codes.question: Attention clause 1: an info code emitted on every detected list; should the expected false-line count be a record field on the PeakList with its help entry, leaving the weak_line flags as the per-line statement?

codes.name: PEAK_KALPHA2_ALIAS
codes.condition: Fires when detection dropped candidates within PEAK_ALIAS_TOL_FWHM_FRAC (0.3) of a FWHM, plus one sampling step, of a stronger candidate's Bragg-predicted Kalpha2 position (indexing/diagnostics.py:402).
codes.measured_on: Synthetic Cu Ka pattern; IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (cpd-4, corundum, thresholds 1.9).
codes.evidence: The Kalpha2 position is physics (the declared wavelengths); the 0.3 tolerance is rietx's. **Removes a line:** the candidates are dropped before any fit and never enter the list. Unanimity: a dissenter exists, a refiner whose genuine weak line aliases onto a Kalpha2 position, which is why the positions are reported.

codes.name: PEAK_KALPHA2_RESIDUAL
codes.condition: Fires on components at a strong group-mate's predicted Kalpha2 maximum, within the mate's own FWHM, at a few per cent of its area (indexing/diagnostics.py:191; pick.py:611).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer) (3 % of area, WP-1028 census).
codes.evidence: The position is predicted from the declared doublet splitting, so the statistic is physics; the area bound is rietx's. Reported, not removed: info and nothing moves, although its suggestion says to exclude the component before indexing.

codes.name: PEAK_LIST_TOO_SHORT
codes.condition: Fires at warning when the list has fewer than PEAK_MIN_USABLE_LINES (20) usable lines (indexing/diagnostics.py:97).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (fluorite, 18 lines).
codes.evidence: The threshold is de Wolff's (1968) M20 definition. The code takes no act of its own; the cap is INDEX_PANEL_REDUCED's. Its help title and description (help.py:3830) still say the list has 'fewer usable lines than an indexing search needs', which WP-1043 made untrue: the search runs and only the scoring needs twenty, as the message itself says.
codes.question: Fix the stale help text, and keep one of PEAK_LIST_TOO_SHORT and INDEX_PANEL_REDUCED (same fact, same threshold, two layers)?

codes.name: PEAK_NOT_SEPARABLE
codes.condition: Fires on components flagged `not_separable`: a re-seed component that is a satellite of a group-mate (within PEAK_SATELLITE_NEAR_FWHM 1.5, area ratio under PEAK_SATELLITE_MAX_RATIO 0.25) in a group whose fit is still refuted at PEAK_REFUTED_SIGMA (3) (indexing/diagnostics.py:131; pick.py:437-460).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (satellite ratios 0.08-0.14); NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer).
codes.evidence: The three-condition test is rietx's own; the thresholds are its satellite constants. **Removes a line:** `not_separable` is in PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS, so the component is withheld from every engine and screen while it stays in the model. Unanimity: no named dissenter for withholding a residual-seeded satellite of a refuted fit, though WP-1043's tail census found real lines this family of screens catches. Its help text says 'did not survive the nested comparison', where the code's load-bearing condition is that the group fit is still refuted.

codes.name: PEAK_NO_INTENSITY
codes.condition: Fires on components flagged `no_intensity`: on the fit's zero-intensity bound, under PEAK_NO_INTENSITY_SIGMA of their own esd, or marked by hand (indexing/diagnostics.py:350).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (6 of 798 lines, thresholds 1.7).
codes.evidence: Already tiered (tier 1, Yue, #993 round 2, 2026-10-21): a record of the flag; the threshold is PEAK_NO_INTENSITY_SIGMA's own row. The flag removes the line from usable() (PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS); that removal is the flag's and its constant's act, not this code's.

codes.name: PEAK_POSITION_AT_BOUND
codes.condition: Fires on components whose fitted 2theta ended on its box bound, PEAK_POSITION_BOUND_FWHM (0.5) of the window's seed FWHM from the seed (indexing/diagnostics.py:319).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (19 usable above-bar components freed on 16 Oct, 12 moved away and 7 towards the lattice line).
codes.evidence: Already tiered (tier 1, Yue, #993 round 2, 2026-10-21): a record of the flag; the bound is PEAK_POSITION_BOUND_FWHM's own row, and the line stays usable.

codes.name: PEAK_POSITION_PRECISION
codes.condition: Fires on every list with a finite median sigma(Q)/Q, at warning above 0.3 x MAX_RELATIVE_SIGMA_Q and at info below (indexing/diagnostics.py:634-650).
codes.measured_on: NIST SRM 660c LaB6 (lab Cu Ka, analyzer); IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a); APS 11-BM NAC (synchrotron); GSAS-II LabData fluorapatite (lab); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase)
codes.evidence: The statistic is arithmetic on the fitted or assumed sigma. The level is split by an inline threshold whose free factor 0.3 has no comment or source, which the rule forbids ('never a threshold between levels'). It moves no search or grade.
codes.question: Should the level split at 0.3 x MAX_RELATIVE_SIGMA_Q go, leaving the numbers in DataQualityReport (relative_sigma_q_median, sigma_over_spacing) as record fields and no diagnostic that fires on every run?

codes.name: PEAK_SHOULDER_SEEDED
codes.condition: Fires when detection offered curvature seeds for components with no local maximum, which Delta-BIC then kept or dropped (indexing/diagnostics.py:412).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a).
codes.evidence: Reports an act on by default (`shoulders=True`): seeding adds candidate components the BIC comparison may keep as usable lines. The comparison's threshold is tiered on its own row. Info; the suggestion names the switch to see the list without them.

codes.name: PEAK_SIGMA_ASSUMED
codes.condition: Fires at warning when the list's `source` is 'positions', so every sigma(2theta) is PEAK_ASSUMED_ESD_DEG (0.02 deg) rather than fitted (indexing/diagnostics.py:109).
codes.measured_on: Bethanechol positions (acceptance test_a_bare_position_list_says_its_sigma_was_assumed); hl2 bare position list (unknown phase).
codes.evidence: Arithmetic on `PeakList.source`; the assumed value is PEAK_ASSUMED_ESD_DEG's own row. Warning matches the rule's definition, since the cell esd a positions-only run reports is computed from that assumed sigma. Only `peak_diagnostics` emits it, called by the GUI's peak editor and `pick_peaks` on lists that are not positions, so `index_pattern` on a `PeakList.from_positions` list never shows it (quality.py:415-418; WP-2013 entry).
codes.question: Should `index_pattern` (or `assess_peak_list`) emit PEAK_SIGMA_ASSUMED, naming the assumed sigma, for a positions list, since that is the only path a positions list actually takes?

codes.name: PEAK_UNRESOLVED_SHOULDER
codes.condition: Fires on components kept in a group where they never separated from a neighbour by half a FWHM (indexing/diagnostics.py:120).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a).
codes.evidence: Reports a flag; the line stays usable and its sigma carries the penalty (PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS deliberately omits it). The half-FWHM separation is rietx's. Info, and nothing moves.

codes.name: PEAK_UNRESOLVED_SPLIT
codes.condition: Fires on comparable components (area ratio at least PEAK_SATELLITE_MAX_RATIO 0.25) closer than Sparrow's limit for the group's fitted shape; each pair is reported as one line with a widened sigma (indexing/diagnostics.py:144).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (789 to 782 usable over 16 patterns); synthetic flat-topped silicon (#728, 34 to 18).
codes.evidence: The statistic is Sparrow's resolution criterion for the fitted shape (peakfit.unresolved_mates). The 0.25 ratio is rietx's. **Removes a line:** the merged component is `unresolved_split`, in PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS, and the stronger one's sigma is widened to reach it. Unanimity: yes, none found, for not offering two lines no shape can resolve.

codes.name: PEAK_WIDTH_CAPPED
codes.condition: Fires on components whose fitted width ran into the upper bound, PEAK_WIDTH_BOUND_FACTORS[1] (5) times the group's seed width (indexing/diagnostics.py:158).
codes.measured_on: IUCr CPD QPA round-robin qarr lab Cu Ka patterns (one source; corundum SRM 676a, zincite, zircon, brucite, magnetite, fluorite, cpd-1a) (6 components, all I/sigma <= 3.9); synthetic steep-background silicon (#728, 129).
codes.evidence: A bound hit is arithmetic; the factor 5 is rietx's. **Removes a line:** `width_capped` is in PEAK_UNUSABLE_FLAGS. Unanimity: no, a refiner indexing a broad second phase or a nanocrystalline line would keep a hump the law calls too wide, and the code's suggestion says to pick it separately.

codes.name: PEAK_WIDTH_LAW_MISMATCH
codes.condition: Fires when the median FWHM of the PEAK_WIDTH_CENSUS_N (12) most prominent lines differs from the instrument law's (indexing path) or the fitted model's (refinement path) by WIDTH_MISMATCH_RATIO (3) or more either way (indexing/diagnostics.py:389, :483).
codes.measured_on: Third-party lab data (WP-1028 census); the ProfileTCHZ default on lab data (ratio near 13); #249's refinement.
codes.evidence: Rank-then-measure on twelve lines is rietx's (WP-1028); the factor 3 is chosen loose on purpose (diagnostics.py:62-67). Broadened specimen or wrong instrument depends on facts outside the pattern, so the code names both readings (third kind). Warning; on the indexing path detection rescales seeds and windows by `width_scale` whatever the ratio. Unanimity on the warning: no, a refiner of a nanocrystalline specimen broadened more than threefold reads it as the finding it is.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity.MAX_AMBIGUITY_INDEX
constants.decides: The highest derivative-lattice index the ambiguity search enumerates, so which supercell partners can be reported and can write the refuting geometric_ambiguity caveat.
constants.evidence: A fence argued from the HNF count (7, 13, 35 at index 2, 3, 4) and Mighell & Santoro (1975) tabulating low-index cases only, which names the source but does not test the cut at 4 (ambiguity.py:88). tests/test_indexing_reduce.py:1277 pins the value and no test shows the report says that partners above index 4 were not looked for, so the tier-1 listing-cap ground is not met.
constants.question: Should the result state the fence (no partner above index 4 sought), which would make it a tier-1 cap on distance, or is index 4 a tier-3 choice to keep?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity.AMBIGUITY_DISCREPANCY_SLACK
constants.decides: How much worse a derivative partner's mean |ΔQ| may be than its parent's and still be reported as explaining the lines equally well, which writes geometric_ambiguity (a refuting caveat) on the parent.
constants.evidence: Argued as a deliberately permissive screen, made safe by extras_absent_in_range doing the refutation (ambiguity.py:286-291); no citation and no measurement in the tree. Unanimity: reporting a partner that fits as well is a second-kind ranking, and no competent refiner would hide one, but the 1.5 factor itself decides which partners exist and so which parents grade low.
constants.question: Is 1.5 measured anywhere (WP-1446/1449), or only argued?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity.MAX_DISCRIMINATING
constants.decides: How many discriminating reflections are listed per partner as advice on where to look; the partner, its verdict and the grade do not read the list.
constants.evidence: The list fills AmbiguityPartner.discriminating_reflections only (ambiguity.py:293-299, 349), and the one other reader prints it as a suggestion (diagnostics.py:729-736), so no candidate, rank or grade moves with it. No test asserts that invariance yet.
constants.question: Accept invariant on the code reading, or require a test asserting rank and grade do not move?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity.AMBIGUITY_EXTEND_FACTOR
constants.decides: How far past the measured 2θ range a partner's discriminating reflections are predicted, as a factor on two_theta_max.
constants.evidence: It sets only tt_ext for the advice list (ambiguity.py:253, 293), so it changes which reflections are suggested and never whether a partner is reported; tests/test_indexing_reduce.py:847 checks the bound, not the invariance.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity._DERIVATIVE_VOLUME_RTOL
constants.decides: Which candidate pairs are tried as parent and derivative by volume ratio, a prefilter before _same_reduced_metric decides.
constants.measured_on: the IUCr round-robin brucite pattern (WP-1446), one family
constants.evidence: Measured once: brucite's a×2 supercell sits 6 ppm from 4× the truth's volume, four orders inside 1 % (ambiguity.py:355-365). A prefilter that never drops a related pair would be answer-invariant, but no test shows the volume error of two independent fits stays under 1 % on a lower-quality cell.
constants.question: Would a test over the acceptance corpus's derivative pairs (largest volume-ratio error found) let this move to invariant?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.ambiguity.SUPERCELL_CHANCE_ALPHA
constants.decides: The significance level below which a containment child's extra lines are seen more often than chance, which separates supercell_refuted (refuting, ranked below its parent) from supported or undecided.
constants.measured_on: the indexing acceptance corpus's finished searches: IUCr round robin, SRM 660c LaB6, GSAS tutorial FAP/NAC (WP-1449)
constants.evidence: A convention placed between measured clusters, correct cells at p ≤ 0.0072 and wrong ones at p ≥ 0.27 (ambiguity.py:456-464); the truth side is close (pseudo-tetragonal LaB6 at 2 of 3 extras), now undecided since thresholds 1.7. Unanimity: none found who would keep a supercell whose extras are seen at chance rate, but the margin on the truth side is a factor 1.4.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.consensus.CONSENSUS_CHECK_TOP
constants.decides: Which candidates get the expensive checks (ambiguity enumeration and the whole-pattern validation fit): the top three plus every candidate an engine consensus could promote (consensus.py:94, checked_indices).
constants.measured_on: not measured (cost per fit ~0.6 s quoted in the comment)
constants.evidence: A cap on which candidates are checked, built so it never removes a candidate the gate could call high: tests/test_indexing_consensus.py:518-529 (test_the_expensive_checks_cover_every_promotable_candidate) asserts the promotable set is always inside it. Unchecked candidates are floored by geometric_ambiguity and carry no validation record, which the result shows per candidate.
constants.question: Is this tier 1 as a cap whose report is complete inside it (every promotable candidate checked, tested), or tier 3 because under a binding ceiling more checked candidates compete for the validation reserve and the validation records a reader sees for ranks 1-3 depend on it (consensus.py:94)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.diagnostics.WIDTH_MISMATCH_RATIO
constants.decides: The measured-to-predicted FWHM ratio past which PEAK_WIDTH_LAW_MISMATCH warns and seed_widths re-seeds the instrument's Gaussian w before validation (workflow.py:375-395).
constants.evidence: Argued between ordinary sample broadening of 2-3× and the ProfileTCHZ default left on lab data, which lands near 13 (diagnostics.py:62-68); no family measurement is cited. Unanimity for the re-seed: none found who would validate lab candidates against a synchrotron line width, and the threshold, not the action, is on trial.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.diagnostics.LAB_LINE_TOLERANCE_ANGSTROM
constants.decides: How far a declared wavelength may sit from one anode's Kα1, Kα2 or weighted mean and still be read as that laboratory source.
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: the six anodes' lines are at least 0.143 Å apart (Fe Kα1 to Co Kα2), so 5e-4 Å names one anode at most while admitting four-decimal typing (1.5405 is 9e-5 off) (diagnostics.py:493-499); tests/test_indexing_quality.py exercises it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.diagnostics.BRAGG_BRENTANO_CELL_PPM
constants.decides: The cell systematic quoted in the info code INDEX_CELL_SYSTEMATIC_UNQUANTIFIED for a Bragg-Brentano cell; it gates nothing.
constants.measured_on: one lab pattern (tag guillemot-study, audit_tools.py check A)
constants.evidence: Measured on one pattern by sweeping goniometer radius 180-320 mm: Rwp moves 0.029 points and about ±85 ppm lands on the lattice parameters (diagnostics.py:687-699). Under three families; the number reaches only an info message (diagnostics.py:951-965).
constants.question: Should the message name the one pattern it was measured on, as the rule asks for a single-family threshold?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_ANGLE_COSINE
constants.decides: The obliquity bound of the dichotomy's search domain: reciprocal angles outside 30-150 degrees are pruned (dichotomy.py:107, read by _initial_box, _inside_domain and _stage_edges).
constants.evidence: Geometry: every lattice's reciprocal lattice has a Buerger-reduced basis with |cos| of each angle at most 1/2, so a bound at cos 30 degrees leaves every lattice reachable in some setting. tests/test_indexing_kernels.py:187 and tests/test_indexing_engines.py:635-740 hold the cone the search enforces, but no test sweeps reduced cells against it.
constants.question: Is the reduced-reciprocal-basis argument the maintainer's reading of 'covers every reduced cell' (dichotomy.py:102), and should a test assert it, given the bound is not stated in any result field?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_DEPTH
constants.decides: How many bisections one box may undergo before it is sent to the assign-refine loop as it stands (dichotomy.py:112, used at :1286).
constants.evidence: A termination guard: reaching it accepts the box as a leaf rather than dropping it, so the search stays exhaustive. In a 6-D triclinic box, 60 bisections are about 10 per dimension (1e-3 of each width), not 1e-18, and the comment at dichotomy.py:1107-1115 records the cap binding in monoclinic under a 3-sigma stopping rule; no test reaches it today.
constants.question: Is a cap that hands the box on rather than dropping it a tier-1 termination guarantee, and does the 'unreachable' wording (dichotomy.py:111) need the per-dimension figure?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_ASSIGN_PASSES
constants.decides: How many assign-refine passes a dichotomy leaf takes before its assignment is reported as it stands (dichotomy.py:117, _accept at :1469-1479).
constants.measured_on: GSAS-II fluorapatite list (WP-2066) and the #1258 381-line list
constants.evidence: rietx's own: WP-2066 measured two closing passes stopping the true fluorapatite cell at 128 of 135 lines where a settled assignment reaches 131 (dichotomy.py:1475-1478). Fewer than three unrelated families, and no test pins the value.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.ANNEAL_FACTOR
constants.decides: How fast the dichotomy's match window tightens from a box's width to the per-line sigma, which decides whether a leaf polishes onto the true cell (dichotomy.py:122, :1469).
constants.measured_on: certified corundum (SRM 676a) per dichotomy.py:1440-1446; not otherwise recorded
constants.evidence: rietx's own schedule; the comment says a gentler schedule bought no measured gain, without naming the datasets. No test pins it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.ACCEPT_SPACING_FRAC
constants.decides: Below what fraction of the median observed-line gap a box stops being bisected and is refined (dichotomy.py:127, :1121).
constants.evidence: rietx's own stopping rule: exhaustiveness rests on the pruning, but whether a leaf's centre polishes onto the truth depends on it; the comment records the 3-sigma alternative never terminating. One family recorded and no test.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.AXIS_STEP
constants.decides: The top-level grid step, 0.4 Angstrom in a principal d-spacing, of the dichotomy's staged grid (dichotomy.py:129, _stage_edges at :595).
constants.evidence: Altomare et al. (2019), International Tables Vol. H ch. 3.4 section 3.4.3.1.5, the DICVOL step the module cites (dichotomy.py:6, :128).
constants.question: Is the grid step answer-invariant (the pruning below it is exact), which would make it invariant rather than tier 2 once a test shows it?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.ANGLE_STEP_DEG
constants.decides: The top-level grid step, 5 degrees of reciprocal angle, of the dichotomy's staged grid (dichotomy.py:131, :608).
constants.evidence: Same source as AXIS_STEP: International Tables Vol. H ch. 3.4 section 3.4.3.1.5, the DICVOL step (dichotomy.py:130).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_TRIAL_HKL
constants.decides: How many trial hkl the dichotomy holds; the widest centrings are dropped past it and the system is reported incomplete (dichotomy.py:136, :1065-1080).
constants.evidence: A memory cap of rietx's own, reported as search_complete = False; tests/test_indexing_engines.py:533-561 holds that the F set survives where P is dropped. Same shape as MAX_GRID_BYTES, approved tier 3 on 2026-10-31.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_GRID_CELLS
constants.decides: How many grid cells the breadth-first pass may hold before the grid is reported incomplete (dichotomy.py:141, :983).
constants.evidence: A memory cap of rietx's own; overflow returns search_complete = False and INDEX_SEARCH_INCOMPLETE rather than truncating. MAX_GRID_BYTES, its companion, was approved tier 3 on 2026-10-31.
constants.question: No test overflows the cell count itself (the bytes cap's test is tests/test_indexing_engines.py:932): should one be built before the row is recorded?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_GRID_BYTES
constants.decides: How many bytes of survivor lists the grid's next stage may hold before the grid is reported incomplete (dichotomy.py:148).
constants.evidence: Current tier 3, approved 2026-10-31 (_audit.py:2384): rietx's own memory bound, reported as INDEX_SEARCH_INCOMPLETE; tests/test_indexing_engines.py::test_the_grid_frontier_is_bounded_by_its_lists_bytes.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.DEDUP_EVERY
constants.decides: How many raw leaves accumulate before an intermediate dedup pass runs between systems (dichotomy.py:152, :849).
constants.evidence: rietx's own memory bound; the comment says it does not change the answer, but no test shows dedup of a partial list then the rest equals dedup of the whole, and a chi-squared equality is not transitive.
constants.question: Should an invariance test (with its margin) move this to invariant?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy.MAX_HARVEST
constants.decides: How many accepted leaves one system unit may hold before it stops and is reported incomplete (dichotomy.py:159).
constants.evidence: Current tier 3, approved 2026-10-31 (_audit.py:2396): rietx's own memory and dedup-time bound, reported as INDEX_SEARCH_INCOMPLETE, and held by tests/test_indexing_engines.py::test_a_dichotomy_unit_stops_at_its_harvest_cap (line 959).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy._FACE_LETTERS
constants.decides: Which axis each face-centring letter's centred face is normal to (dichotomy.py:234).
constants.evidence: Definition: A, B and C centrings are named for the face normal to a, b and c.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy._OFFDIAG_PARTNERS
constants.decides: Which diagonal A..F components pair with each off-diagonal one in the Cauchy-Schwarz bound (dichotomy.py:569).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic read off qspace._AF_INDEX: D = 2G*23 pairs (B, C), E pairs (A, C), F pairs (A, B).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.dichotomy._SAME_BOX_RTOL
constants.decides: On what relative grid a converged box's A..F is hashed, so that a second leaf in the same cell is skipped before refinement (dichotomy.py:1330, :1362).
constants.evidence: rietx's own pre-filter; tests/test_indexing_engines.py:813-840 holds that cells 20 tolerances apart hash apart and 0.1 apart hash together. A skipped leaf is skipped, not merged, so two cells within 0.1 % that a synchrotron chi-squared would separate are not both refined.
constants.question: Is 1e-3 safely coarser than nothing the dedup would keep apart, given CELL_EQUALITY_CHI2 can separate cells far closer than this on synchrotron data?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.MAX_PREDICTED_REFLECTIONS
constants.decides: Refuses a trial cell whose predicted reflection count exceeds two million rather than enumerating it, before every generate_reflections a search reaches (engines.py:82, reflection_ceiling_ok).
constants.measured_on: not measured on a family; a runaway synthetic cell in tests/test_indexing_engines.py:374
constants.evidence: A crash guard (the module docstring's 1.6 PiB case): two million triples is ~48 MB, and the comment says no legitimate cell in a bounded search reaches it. tests/test_indexing_engines.py:374 shows a runaway cell exceeds it; no test shows that every cell inside the default box (max_d_axis 25 Å) at the shortest bundled wavelength stays below it.
constants.question: Should a test pin that the largest default-box cell at 11-BM NAC's 0.414 Å and its 2θ range predicts fewer than MAX_PREDICTED_REFLECTIONS, so the guard is shown never to refuse a reachable cell (engines.py:82)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEDUP_VOLUME_RTOL
constants.decides: Skips the χ² lattice-equality test for two candidates whose reduced volumes differ by more than 1 % (engines.py:88, _dedup_admits).
constants.measured_on: bethanechol set F and qarr corundum harvests (WP-1509), synthetic twins
constants.evidence: A gate on comparisons whose answer is already known, measured to change no group: tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1369 (test_the_fast_dedup_groups_exactly_as_the_plain_pass) builds cousins inside the gate and twins the χ² merges across 0.6 % of volume and asserts every group, its order and members equal the plain pass.
constants.question: The invariance rests on the χ² never merging two lattices more than 1 % apart in volume; is that bounded for a candidate with a very large cov_af, or should the test add one (engines.py:88)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEDUP_STACK_FIRST
constants.decides: Size of the first stack of χ² tests in dedup, each later stack four times the last (engines.py:93).
constants.evidence: The comment says it moves the clock, never a verdict, and tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1505 (test_the_stacked_dedup_groups_exactly_as_one_pair_at_a_time, reading the constant at :1559) asserts the stacked pass builds the plain pass's groups with a match in the first stack, the second, none, and the cache.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MIN_D_AXIS
constants.decides: The shortest principal d(100) a search considers, the lower edge of every engine's Q-space box (engines.py:99).
constants.evidence: rietx's own bound with a stated geometric meaning (a bound on d(100) = a sin β, not on a) and no measurement or program default in the repo; docs/practice.md records DICVOL06's volume range from the user but no axis default.
constants.question: A hexagonal cell's d(100) is a·√3/2, so any hexagonal metric with a below about 2.31 Å is outside the default box; beryllium's a is about 2.29 Å by recall (not checked against a source in the repo). Is that case real, and should the floor sit lower (engines.py:99)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MAX_D_AXIS
constants.decides: The longest principal d-spacing a search considers, the upper edge of the box every engine searches (engines.py:103).
constants.measured_on: bethanechol published peak sets (longest axis 15.9 Å)
constants.evidence: rietx's own: the comment justifies 25 Å by small-molecule organics and the bethanechol benchmark's 15.9 Å axis, one family. A cell with a longer axis is never found and the result does not say the box excluded it beyond spec_notes.
constants.question: Is there an indexing program default for the longest axis in the repo's survey (docs/practice.md has none), and should a run whose envelope exceeds the box say so (engines.py:103)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MIN_VOLUME
constants.decides: The smallest cell volume a search reports; engines drop a fitted cell below 15 Å³ (engines.py:107, trial_error.py:518, svd.py:969).
constants.evidence: Stated as physics (smaller than one atom's exclusion volume) but the comparison is on the fitted cell in its searched system and centring, so a one-atom primitive metallic cell (about 11.8 Å³ for Cu or Fe, by recall) would be refused in a triclinic or rhombohedral-primitive search while its centred cubic description passes. No test or source in the repo bounds the value.
constants.question: Is the floor physics (tier 1) as the comment claims, given that primitive cells of common metals sit below it and are only found through a centred setting (engines.py:107)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_SEARCH_LINES
constants.decides: How many observed lines drive a search (the strongest N from a low-Q pool); scoring then uses every usable line (engines.py:140).
constants.measured_on: the known-cell corpus swept by WP-1039 (NIST SRM 660c, qarr, 11-BM NAC, GSAS-II FAP)
constants.evidence: The indexing engines' published defaults sit at twenty: DICVOL06 card 2 N "e.g. N = 20" (dicvol06.inf:83-91), TREOR90 USE defaults to 19 with a maximum of 20, McMaille's automatic mode takes twenty, and Bergmann et al. (2004) gave every program the first 20 lines (docs/practice.md:681-713). Conograph's 48 is the named dissenter; WP-1039 measured that raising N bought nothing on the corpus, and which twenty (SEARCH_POOL_MULTIPLE) is rietx's own.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SEARCH_POOL_MULTIPLE
constants.decides: The low-Q pool, as a multiple of n_search_lines, from which the strongest driven lines are drawn (engines.py:164).
constants.measured_on: WP-1039: 11-BM NAC, qarr corundum and zircon, NIST SRM 660c, the indexing acceptance file
constants.evidence: Not answer-invariant: the comment measures NAC's driven truth lines 20 to 18, corundum 19 to 17, zircon 18 to 17 against the unbounded rule, every acceptance row passing either way, and the cost 72 s to 26 s on corundum's trigonal unit. Three unrelated families (NIST lab, qarr lab, 11-BM synchrotron); no program ranks the driven lines by intensity (docs/practice.md:725-733), so the rule sits outside existing practice and names its reason.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_N_UNINDEXED
constants.decides: How many driven lines a cell may leave unindexed and still be accepted on the default first pass, and on a list with no anchor (engines.py:173, SearchSpec.miss_budget).
constants.measured_on: not measured as a value; the inlier retry's measurements are on synthetic Si
constants.evidence: The comment cites DICVOL06's reported gain from an impurity tolerance but names no DICVOL default count, and Bergmann et al. (2004) record manual runs tolerating 8-10 unindexed lines (docs/practice.md:717). The value 2 is rietx's own, with the failure case stated (more off-lattice lines than the cap complete as no cell, fixed by the inlier retry).
constants.question: Does DICVOL06's manual give a default count of impurity lines (dicvol06.inf), which would make the default tier 2 if 2 sits inside the programs' range (engines.py:173)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.INLIER_FRACTION
constants.decides: Under the inlier rule, the fraction of driven lines a cell must index to be accepted, used on the retry after a first pass finds no agreement (engines.py:205).
constants.measured_on: one synthetic Si pattern with twelve planted lines; SRM 660c LaB6 for the retry-only ruling
constants.evidence: rietx's own on one synthetic family: 0.6 is that measurement's 12 of 20, 0.7 and 0.75 lose the truth there. Le Bail (2004, Powder Diffr. 19, 249)'s under-35 %-impurity bound is the published range it sits inside, and the retry-after-silence shape has precedent (Bergmann et al. 2004, DICVOL91's advice, docs/practice.md:730-731).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.INLIER_DOF_MARGIN
constants.decides: Inliers beyond the metric's degrees of freedom the inlier rule requires; binds only on short lists (engines.py:211).
constants.evidence: Fischler and Bolles (1981)'s RANSAC acceptance gives the shape (a minimal subset plus verification), not the number four; a paper that tests a formula does not test the numbers inside it (generality.md § The rule, 2026-11-05).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.ANCHOR_LINES
constants.decides: How many of the strongest driven lines every accepted cell must index, also a prune for the exhaustive engine (engines.py:222).
constants.measured_on: one synthetic Si pattern (8 anchors put a planted line among them)
constants.evidence: rietx's own, one synthetic family; a position-only list has no anchor and keeps DEFAULT_N_UNINDEXED. A cell missing one of the five strongest lines is never returned, an action whose dissenter would be a refiner whose strongest line is an impurity's.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DRIVEN_MIN_LINES
constants.decides: The fewest driven lines before a line carrying an undriven flag is taken back into the driven set (engines.py:228).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic, already in the table: the triclinic reciprocal metric has six components, so fewer than six driven lines cannot determine every lattice a search may be asked for (_audit.py:2422).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_SHIFT_DEG
constants.decides: The systematic 2θ allowance added in quadrature to every line's σ when no shift is measured, the cap on the width-derived allowance (engines.py:266).
constants.measured_on: qarr corundum (SRM 676a), NIST SRM 660c (where 0.060° manufactured a wrong high cell)
constants.evidence: The indexing programs' default matching windows bracket it: DICVOL06 0.03° 2θ (dicvol06.inf:139-157), ITO15 TOLG 0.06° (ito15.inf:337-342), TOPAS index_max_th2_error 0.05° (inferred from a summarised manual fetch), docs/practice.md:279-286; a value between two programs' values is inside the range. Every result reports it as INDEX_SHIFT_ALLOWANCE, and shift_allowance_assumed keeps high unreachable on real data.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.WIDTH_ALLOWANCE_FWHM
constants.decides: When the pair screen declines on a picked list, the allowance is this multiple of the usable lines' lower-quartile FWHM, capped at DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_SHIFT_DEG (engines.py:290, width_allowance).
constants.measured_on: one synthetic Si twin of F2's T5 arms (λ 0.8257 Å, FWHM 0.021°)
constants.evidence: rietx's own on one synthetic family; no surveyed program scales its window with the peak width (docs/practice.md:292-293), so the choice sits outside practice and names its reason (the 0.05° window is two to six FWHM on high-resolution data). It needs the inlier rule, and the shift stays unmeasured and reported.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.WIDTH_ALLOWANCE_QUANTILE
constants.decides: Which quantile of the usable lines' FWHM the width allowance multiplies (engines.py:293).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, argued (the picker's junk components are the broad ones) and measured only jointly with WIDTH_ALLOWANCE_FWHM on one synthetic family.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS
constants.decides: Wall-clock seconds one (engine × system) unit may spend before it stops and reports search_complete false (engines.py:296).
constants.measured_on: WP-1042 corpus re-measure; bethanechol set F (WP-1046); #1374's synthetic monoclinic and orthorhombic lists
constants.evidence: Not answer-invariant: a truncated unit can omit the truth or a finder, and WP-1046 measured a cap interacting with it (bethanechol set F's truth present at 5 s and 15 s, absent at 30 s and 60 s before the pool fix). No program default in the repo (DICVOL04 runs to 3770 s); under quick, #1374 measured the 30 s slice never worse than a ceiling-sized unit on 15 rows.
constants.question: Issue #1374 asks whether a declared ceiling should cap each unit at a share, min(budget_seconds, T_search / n_engines), since one unit can hold the whole ceiling when a caller raises budget_seconds to it; adopt it, and per engine or over the remaining units (engines.py:296)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES
constants.decides: How many candidates the reported list holds after consensus ranks the whole merge; it also bounds what estimate_ceiling prices and checked_indices may reach (engines.py:316).
constants.measured_on: bethanechol set F (WP-1046); a synthetic cubic list in tests/test_indexing_consensus.py:499-515
constants.evidence: A listing cap applied once, at the layer whose ordering is authoritative (WP-1046 moved it off the units). tests/test_indexing_consensus.py:505-515 asserts the list holds exactly the cap and INDEX_CANDIDATES_TRUNCATED states the truncation, whose message counts the merged lattices left out.
constants.question: Two doubts on tier 1: the test asserts the truncation note fires but not its count, and WP-2112 (#1375) reports an engine's own first cell dropped from the twelve because every corroborated cell sorts above it, so the cut decides what a reader sees when the gate abstains. Is that a ranking-key question for WP-2112 or a reason to tier the cap 3 (engines.py:316)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.ENGINE_POOL_MULTIPLE
constants.decides: How many candidates each (engine × system) unit hands to the merge, as a multiple of max_candidates (engines.py:331, SearchSpec.engine_pool).
constants.evidence: rietx's own on one family: five makes the default pool the measured 60, at which set F's truth returns ranked 3rd; a pool of 200 cost 91.6 s against 90.7 s at 12. Smaller multiples were not measured, and a cut above the ranking layer is a ranking (WP-1046), so the pool decides what consensus can rank; INDEX_CANDIDATES_TRUNCATED flags it at the pool.
constants.question: Should a second and third family (a low-symmetry synthetic list, a qarr pattern) measure that the truth survives the unit pool before the multiple is kept (engines.py:331)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.MIN_AGREEMENT
constants.decides: How many engines must find a lattice for it to count as corroborated: grade floors fewer at low before any caveat is read, rank_candidates sorts corroborated first, and _no_agreement triggers the inlier retry (engines.py:337).
constants.measured_on: FAP (GSAS-II tutorial; the cross-code cell leads since WP-1046), bethanechol (finder counts not comparable across systems)
constants.evidence: rietx's own design (engines that fail differently must agree, indexing/CLAUDE.md § The governing rule); no established program requires two engines. As an ordering it is a second-kind ranking key; as the grade floor it is an action, and a refiner who indexes with one program (DICVOL or TOPAS alone) and accepts a single-program solution on M20 is a named dissenter to that floor.
constants.question: With a dissenter named, should the floor at low stay an action (the grade is rietx's own confidence vocabulary and the candidate stays listed) or be reported only as the agreement count beside the ranking (engines.py:337, consensus.grade)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.PROVISIONAL_STREAM_TOP
constants.decides: How many cells a just-finished (engine × system) unit streams as provisional events, with no confidence field (engines.py:820).
constants.evidence: Presentation only by construction: its one reader is provisional_payload, the streamed events carry no grade, and the returned IndexingResult does not read them.
constants.question: No test asserts that the final result is the same at any value; is the construction enough, or should the invariance test be added (engines.py:820)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines._INDEX_MAX_CONDITION
constants.decides: The largest Σ|A..F|/λ_min(G*) at which TrialIndex bounds a cell's rows rather than scanning the whole set (engines.py:887).
constants.evidence: A numerical floor with its rounding bound derived in the comment (6.7e-10 of Q against a 1e-6 margin). tests/test_indexing_engines.py:433 (test_the_trial_index_keeps_every_row_a_cell_can_put_in_range_in_order) asserts every needed row is kept, in order, over at least 300 restricted cases.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines._INDEX_MIN_DEFECT
constants.decides: The smallest orthogonality defect at which the closed-form inverse of G* is trusted for the row bound (engines.py:894).
constants.evidence: A numerical floor whose rounding (≲ 1.3e-8 of the determinant above it) is derived in the comment; a metric below it takes the whole set. Covered by the same row-completeness test (tests/test_indexing_engines.py:433).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines._INDEX_MARGIN
constants.decides: The relative slack on each per-axis index bound (engines.py:898).
constants.evidence: A numerical margin fifty times the derived rounding; a looser bound costs rows, never correctness, and the row-completeness test (tests/test_indexing_engines.py:433) asserts no needed row is lost.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines._INDEX_MAX_SHARE
constants.decides: The fraction of a trial set above which a bounded row list is not built and the set is scanned whole (engines.py:901).
constants.evidence: A cost switch between two paths that return the same rows in the same order: the restriction keeps a superset of the needed rows in the set's own order (tests/test_indexing_engines.py:433), and WP-1509 replays finished units to their digests (python -m tests.unit_replay).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines._INDEX_MIN_ROWS
constants.decides: The trial-set size below which no row index is built (engines.py:908).
constants.evidence: A cost switch measured for speed (1188 to 138 µs at 150 381 rows); the indexed and scanned paths keep the same rows (tests/test_indexing_engines.py:433, :473 asserts a small set is scanned whole), and row_local_product checks the product's rounding once a process.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_VOLUME_CEILING
constants.decides: The search's volume ceiling when neither the caller nor the data-quality report supplies one for a system (engines.py:1273, search_volume_ceiling).
constants.measured_on: not measured; tests/test_indexing_quality.py:437-465 pins the fallback
constants.evidence: rietx's own, chosen generous to exclude only the absurd; on index_pattern's default path assess_peak_list always runs, so it binds only where a system has no envelope. DICVOL06's default VOLMAX is 2500 Å³ (docs/practice.md:657), so 8000 sits outside the one program default surveyed and names its reason.
constants.question: Does any default path reach this fallback (a system without a volume_envelope entry), or is it reached only by callers passing quality=None to the engines directly (engines.py:1298)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.IDENTITY_CHANGE
constants.decides: The change_of_basis recorded on a candidate whose setting was not changed (engines.py:1632).
constants.evidence: The 3×3 identity matrix, arithmetic.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SAME_SOLUTION_RTOL
constants.decides: The relative grid on which a solved metric is hashed before refinement, so repeated solutions are refined once (engines.py:1681, solution_key).
constants.evidence: Not shown invariant: indexing/CLAUDE.md § More rules records that solution_key's quantised key, claimed before scoring, lost a cubic-I truth and fired INDEX_DOMINANT_ZONE for two years (WP-1041). No test names the value.
constants.question: Should an invariance or sweep test bound the 1e-3 grid against the corpus, since a dedup key claimed before scoring can fail with a wrong answer (engines.py:1681)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.engines.QUICK_TOTAL_BUDGET_SECONDS
