constants.evidence: Read only by estimate_ceiling; it states the worst case and moves no search, rank or grade.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction.DECISIVE_DELTA_BIC
constants.decides: The ΔBIC margin by which the top surviving extinction class must beat the next before ExtinctionScreen.best_or_none returns it (schemas/indexing.py:2653-2660).
constants.evidence: Kass & Raftery (1995) call a difference above 10 very strong evidence, the band the rule itself names as tier 2 (extinction.py:149-153). Note for the best_or_none task: the GUI's extinction route calls screen.best_or_none() (gui/session.py:2803), so this pick margin reaches a default path. The sham probe in the module docstring (corundum SRM 676a, round robin: 40-50 % of sham positions 1-3 FWHM from an allowed line clear 3σ, up to 24.7σ, extinction.py:61-79) measures the absence test's ABSENT_SIGMA (workflow.py:106, outside this slice) on one family only, and the fix it motivated is _model_is_quiet, not a threshold.
constants.question: The GUI route reaches this pick margin: is the GUI's 'best' marker the pick verb the rule allows, or a default that must pass the unanimity gate?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction.REFERENCE_NET_RWP_MAX
constants.decides: The background-subtracted Rwp of the absence-free reference fit above which the screen is marked unreliable and best_or_none abstains, the classes still ranked (extinction.py:1376-1382).
constants.measured_on: one synthetic Si pattern at 11-BM-like resolution with the cell 0.4 % off; a real synchrotron pattern built as a mechanism in tests/test_extinction_gate.py
constants.evidence: The statistic is Toby (2006)'s background-subtracted Rwp, tier 2; the bar 1/√2 (half the net weighted power unexplained) is rietx's, measured on one synthetic case (extinction.py:155-167). Arithmetic in extinction.py:1107-1111 shows a perfect fit reads √(N/(N+S)), so the bar also abstains on weak data (S < N) with no misfit at all, which the message separates (thresholds 1.12). Unanimity for abstaining: none found who would name an extinction symbol from a reference that leaves half the net signal unexplained.
constants.question: One synthetic family only: keep at tier 3 under the rare-feature wording, or ask for a second and third family before the abstention stands?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction.N_A_CM3_PER_A3
constants.decides: The unit factor that turns density, cell volume and formula weight into formula units per cell.
constants.evidence: N_A × 1e-24 cm³/Å³, N_A exact in the SI since 2019 (extinction.py:169-173); tests/test_extinction_prior.py uses it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction.DENSITY_Z_TOLERANCE
constants.decides: How far a declared density may put Z from a whole number (fraction of Z) before it names that Z, filters the members by it, or contradicts a declared z and makes best_or_none abstain.
constants.evidence: International Tables Vol. C (2006) §3.2.1 gives 1.5 % for measured against calculated density (extinction.py:175-186), ruled on PR #1140 (WP-2033). Arithmetic checked against density_zs (extinction.py:502-509): two whole Z first fit at z_rho = 33.49 ({33, 34}), about 35 % of z_rho in 40-50 and 65 % in 50-60 give two, every z_rho ≥ 66 gives at least two, and no whole Z fits up to z_rho = 32.5; so the z_candidates field comment's 'Z ≳ 50' (schemas/indexing.py:2590, not ~2547) should read 'Z ≳ 33', as extinction.py:184 and :531 already say. Z_INTEGER_TOLERANCE no longer exists in the tree: WP-2030 (closed 2026-11-07) deleted it with INDEX_Z_NOT_INTEGER (PR #1237; schemas/indexing.py:218), so it has no row here and WP-2030 owns that rule.
constants.question: Correct schemas/indexing.py:2590 to 'Z ≳ 33' in this WP's code change (not edited by this proposal)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction._ZONES
constants.decides: The vocabulary of the zones (planes through the origin) on which reflection conditions are stated when deriving an extinction class's conditions; each is kept only if it reproduces the absence set exactly.
constants.evidence: Crystallography: the derivation fits conditions to the computed absence set (extinction.py:615-648), and tests/test_extinction_symbol.py:196 measures it over the whole table: 1 of 550 settings (C 4 2 21, non-standard) is incomplete and reports conditions_complete = False rather than a partial list.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction._AXES
constants.decides: The vocabulary of the axes on which reflection conditions are stated when deriving an extinction class's conditions; each is kept only if it reproduces the absence set exactly.
constants.evidence: Crystallography: the derivation fits conditions to the computed absence set (extinction.py:615-648), and tests/test_extinction_symbol.py:196 measures it over the whole table: 1 of 550 settings (C 4 2 21, non-standard) is incomplete and reports conditions_complete = False rather than a partial list.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction._FORMS2
constants.decides: The vocabulary of the linear forms of two free indices tried as conditions when deriving an extinction class's conditions; each is kept only if it reproduces the absence set exactly.
constants.evidence: Crystallography: the derivation fits conditions to the computed absence set (extinction.py:615-648), and tests/test_extinction_symbol.py:196 measures it over the whole table: 1 of 550 settings (C 4 2 21, non-standard) is incomplete and reports conditions_complete = False rather than a partial list.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction._FORMS1
constants.decides: The vocabulary of the linear form of one free index tried as a condition when deriving an extinction class's conditions; each is kept only if it reproduces the absence set exactly.
constants.evidence: Crystallography: the derivation fits conditions to the computed absence set (extinction.py:615-648), and tests/test_extinction_symbol.py:196 measures it over the whole table: 1 of 550 settings (C 4 2 21, non-standard) is incomplete and reports conditions_complete = False rather than a partial list.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.extinction._MODULI
constants.decides: The moduli (2, 3, 4, 6) against which each linear form is tried as a reflection condition.
constants.evidence: Physics: crystallographic translations (centring, glide and screw components) are 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 or 1/6 of a lattice vector, so these are the only moduli a condition can have (extinction.py:644-648); the whole-table test (tests/test_extinction_symbol.py:196) covers it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.fom.MATCH_SIGMA
constants.decides: How many σ_eff an observed and a predicted line may differ by and count as one line, shared by the whole FoM panel, assignment and the ambiguity checks, and SearchSpec.k_sigma's default (fom.py:45).
constants.measured_on: WP-1018's pull ensemble (a single line and a lab doublet)
constants.evidence: rietx's own 3σ on a σ measured to be calibrated (pull mean +0.03, std 0.97; −0.08, 0.98 on a doublet), the same shape as the absent-phase hold's 3σ, which generality.md § The rule puts on trial under the mechanical ground. The families behind WP-1018's pulls are not named in the comment.
constants.question: Is a 3σ window on a calibrated σ tier 1 (Gaussian arithmetic, once the calibration is tested) or tier 3 (a chosen coverage), and which families did WP-1018's pull ensemble use (fom.py:45)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.fom.LINE_COINCIDENCE_RTOL
constants.decides: The relative separation below which two calculated reflections are merged into one line (fom.py:88).
constants.evidence: A numerical floor nine orders below any measurement precision, merging exact coincidences only; tests/test_indexing_screen.py reads it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.fom._BOUNDARY_RTOL
constants.decides: The tie tolerance on the up-to-the-N-th-observed-line boundary in every N_poss count (fom.py:291).
constants.measured_on: one lattice in two unimodular settings (N_poss 20 and 19, M20 76.43 and 80.45 before it)
constants.evidence: A tie rule, not a fudge: the N-th observed line is itself a predicted line, so a strict comparison makes a setting-invariant count depend on rounding. No test names it yet.
constants.question: Should a test pin that M20 and N_poss are equal in two unimodular settings of one lattice (fom.py:291)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.fom.RESOLUTION_FWHM
constants.decides: The resolution multiple for every reversed question: merge distance, seen half-width and p0's scale, in FWHM (fom.py:521).
constants.measured_on: 15 real runs from 12 sources (CPD round robin, NIST SRM 660c, 11-BM NAC, GSAS-II FAP, Hill's PbSO4 X-ray and neutron) and a synthetic tetragonal split
constants.evidence: Already tier 3, kept 2026-10-21 (_audit.py:2498): 1.0 over 0.5 on the synthetic split, and the real-family sweep 0.5-1.0 moved one rank (PbSO4 X-ray at 0.7). Rayleigh (1879) and Sparrow (1916) bracket one-line-or-two at about a width but do not cover the seen window or p0.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.fom._AGGREGATE_FLOOR_RTOL
constants.decides: How far below the best candidate a member's value is floored before its log is taken in the log-sum aggregate (fom.py:907).
constants.evidence: A relative numerical floor that keeps the aggregate unit-invariant. Its only reader, fom._log_sum_scores, is unwired: no module calls it (grep 2026-11-16; consensus.py:663 names it in a docstring) and indexing/CLAUDE.md § Engines and the FoM panel says it stays unwired, so today it moves nothing returned.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peakfit._H_WIDTH
constants.decides: The finite-difference step for the (Γ_G, Γ_L) → (w₁, w₂) width map in the group fitter's Jacobian.
constants.evidence: A numerical setting whose error a test bounds: test_group_jacobian_matches_finite_differences (tests/test_peak_picking.py:299) holds the analytic Jacobian within 5e-5 of central differences on six shapes including true Voigt and asymmetric FCJ.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peakfit._H_POS
constants.decides: The finite-difference step for the FCJ node vectors' motion with position in the group fitter's Jacobian.
constants.evidence: Covered by the same test as _H_WIDTH (tests/test_peak_picking.py:299), whose docstring names the FCJ node-vector differences; worst column within 5e-5.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peakfit._SEED_GAUSS_FRACTION
constants.decides: The Gaussian share of the seed combined width at the start of every group fit.
constants.evidence: Argued (both components must start non-zero; a Gaussian-dominant start avoids over-weighting tails, peakfit.py:100-106); a seed can move which minimum a non-linear fit reaches, and no test shows the converged components are independent of it.
constants.question: Is there a measurement that 0.8 against, say, 0.5 leaves the picked list unchanged, which would make it invariant?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peakfit._SPARROW_DIP_MIN
constants.decides: The relative dip depth below which two equal lines count as one maximum, so whether a pair is mergeable or an unresolved mate.
constants.evidence: Sparrow's criterion is whether a dip exists; 1e-6 only keeps a rounding ripple on a flat top from counting as one (peakfit.py:530-534), a numerical floor. No test pins it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peaks._LN2_8
constants.decides: The factor 8 ln 2 converting a Gaussian variance to its squared FWHM in the shoulder seeds.
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: FWHM² = 8 ln 2 σ² for a Gaussian (peaks.py:63).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peaks.MIN_GROUP_POINTS
constants.decides: The fewest channels a caller-requested window (group_at, the GUI peak editor) may hold before it is refused with a ValueError.
constants.evidence: Argued as enough channels to fit two widths and one component (peaks.py:64-69, 217-222); detection never meets it. No measurement and no test.
constants.question: Is 8 channels arithmetic (twice the four free parameters) and so tier 1, or a choice?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.peaks.TRIAL_GAP_STEPS
constants.decides: The channel step, as a multiple of the median step, read as an excluded gap when counting the resolution elements that set the false-discovery bar.
constants.evidence: No measurement in the tree (peaks.py:496-500); it changes n_trials and so the Benjamini-Hochberg bar of PEAK_FDR_Q on any pattern with excluded regions.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.priors.CLASSIFY_RTOL
constants.decides: The relative axis-equality tolerance used to classify a prior cell's crystal system, which sets where the prior is checked and which system jumps the queue (priors.py:71).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, inside an opt-in (SearchSpec.prior_cells defaults to empty) but used once the switch is on, so tiered on its own (generality.md § Caller, condition 2). A misclassified prior fails its own check; the engines still search every system.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.priors.CLASSIFY_ATOL_DEG
constants.decides: The absolute angle-equality tolerance (deg) used to classify a prior cell's crystal system (priors.py:72).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, inside the opt-in priors and used once a prior is supplied; no comment of its own beyond CLASSIFY_RTOL's.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.priors.MAX_PRIOR_PASSES
constants.decides: How many assign-refine passes a prior cell gets before its assignment is taken as settled (priors.py:76).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, said to match the engines' own leaves; inside the opt-in priors.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.priors.MAX_PRIOR_INDEX
constants.decides: Refuses, loudly, a prior whose longest axis needs more than 40 indices to reach the observed Q range (priors.py:82).
constants.evidence: A guard after the MAX_TRIAL_HKL precedent, inside the opt-in priors; a refused prior is reported rather than capped, but no test or measurement in the repo bounds the value.
constants.question: Is this a tier-1 computational guard (refused and reported), or tier 3 as a number that decides which priors are checked (priors.py:82)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.priors.PRIOR_DRIFT_MAX
constants.decides: The largest relative volume drift a prior's check may take from the stated cell before it stops counting as a check of that cell (priors.py:93).
constants.measured_on: one synthetic pin case (a tetragonal prior on cubic 4.157 Å data)
constants.evidence: rietx's own, one synthetic case: the assign-refine loop walked a wrong prior to the true lattice and called it confirmed. 10 % in volume is about 3 % per axis; the seeded svd start still finds the basin as an engine, so the guard keeps provenance honest and loses no candidate.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.qspace._AF_INDEX
constants.decides: The fixed map giving which G* component each of A..F is, between the quadratic-form coefficients and the reciprocal metric tensor.
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: (A..F) = (G*₁₁, G*₂₂, G*₃₃, 2G*₂₃, 2G*₁₃, 2G*₁₂) by definition of Q(hkl) (qspace.py:55-63); tests/test_indexing_core.py:167 checks the cell Jacobian built on it against finite differences.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.qspace._AF_FACTOR
constants.decides: The fixed map giving the factor of two on A..F's off-diagonal entries, between the quadratic-form coefficients and the reciprocal metric tensor.
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: (A..F) = (G*₁₁, G*₂₂, G*₃₃, 2G*₂₃, 2G*₁₃, 2G*₁₂) by definition of Q(hkl) (qspace.py:55-63); tests/test_indexing_core.py:167 checks the cell Jacobian built on it against finite differences.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.qspace._VOIGT_OF_AF
constants.decides: The fixed map giving the Voigt slot of each A..F entry, between the quadratic-form coefficients and the reciprocal metric tensor.
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: (A..F) = (G*₁₁, G*₂₂, G*₃₃, 2G*₂₃, 2G*₁₃, 2G*₁₂) by definition of Q(hkl) (qspace.py:55-63); tests/test_indexing_core.py:167 checks the cell Jacobian built on it against finite differences.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.quality._LAUE_ORBIT_FACTOR
constants.decides: Reflections per Laue orbit relative to triclinic, scaling Smith's volume envelope per system (quality.py:114).
constants.evidence: Physics: the Laue-class order over the triclinic order, checked against the package's own generate_reflections in tests/test_indexing_quality.py:501 rather than trusted as a table.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.quality._MAX_CENTRING
constants.decides: The largest centring multiplicity each system admits, the worst case the volume envelope uses (quality.py:240).
constants.evidence: Physics: lattice points per conventional cell of the most centred Bravais type of each system (F 4, R in the hexagonal setting 3, I/C 2), asserted in tests/test_indexing_quality.py:477.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.quality.VOLUME_ENVELOPE_SLACK
constants.decides: The factor between Smith's mean-line volume estimate and the search ceiling, and the margin past which consensus reports volume_unphysical (quality.py:254).
constants.measured_on: Smith's own calibration set, as the comment reads it (raw line excludes the truth below p = 0.71)
constants.evidence: Smith's envelope is the cited statistic; 1.5 is a free factor above Smith's worst case (1/0.71 ≈ 1.41), so it is tiered on its own (generality.md § The rule, a factor is a threshold of its own). tests/test_indexing_quality.py:455 pins the ceiling as slack × envelope.
constants.question: Should the slack be measured on the corpus (the fraction of truths whose volume sits above the raw envelope), or does Smith's published worst case make 1.5 tier 2 (quality.py:254)?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.CELL_EQUALITY_CHI2
constants.decides: When two candidates' reduced A..F vectors are one lattice, which merges candidates in every dedup (reduce.py:95).
constants.measured_on: tests/indexing_gallery.py and tests/test_acceptance_indexing.py families: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (corundum, zincite, zircon), GSAS-II fluorapatite tutorial list, bethanechol published sets
constants.evidence: The statistic is a chi-squared on the joint covariance and 16.8119 is the chi-squared(6) 0.99 quantile (arithmetic); the 99 % level is rietx's choice, with no source cited in the repo. tests/test_indexing_reduce.py:347-363 holds that one pair is one lattice at lab precision and two at synchrotron precision.
constants.question: Is a 99 % level established practice for a lattice-equality test (tier 2 with a source), or rietx's own?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.CELL_EQUALITY_RELATIVE
constants.decides: When two candidates without a covariance are one lattice, as a relative bound on A..F (reduce.py:99).
constants.measured_on: tests/indexing_gallery.py and tests/test_acceptance_indexing.py families: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (corundum, zincite, zircon), GSAS-II fluorapatite tutorial list, bethanechol published sets
constants.evidence: rietx's own: set an order looser than a synchrotron cell's precision so it never tightens what chi-squared would decide; tests/test_indexing_plots.py:335-348 holds the truth test tighter than it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.NIGGLI_EPS_RELATIVE
constants.decides: The floating-point tolerance of every comparison inside the Niggli reduction, eps = 1e-5 times V^(1/3) (reduce.py:116).
constants.evidence: A numerical tolerance whose value is Grosse-Kunstleve, Sauter & Adams (2004), Acta Cryst. A60, 1-6, eq. (3), and their Test 3 passes at it; tests/test_indexing_reduce.py::test_niggli_reduction_is_unimodular_invariant reproduces that test here (and :442-449 reads the value).
constants.question: Should the row cite the paper as tier 2 instead, since the cell it treats as metrically special within eps decides a tie?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.BRAVAIS_OBLIQUITIES
constants.decides: The Le Page obliquities (0.5-3 degrees) swept by bravais_screen, whose loosest value decides INDEX_BRAVAIS_AMBIGUOUS and whose tightest decides the reported system (reduce.py:118, :300).
constants.evidence: rietx's own sweep over Le Page's (1982) method; tests/test_indexing_reduce.py:180-189 holds monotonicity across it but no source in the repo gives the values.
constants.question: Does an established program's Le Page default (PLATON, gemmi) sit inside 0.5-3 degrees, which would make it tier 2?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.BRAVAIS_SYMPREC_SIGMAS
constants.decides: The multiples of the cell's own esd used as spglib symprec values in bravais_screen (reduce.py:123).
constants.evidence: rietx's own; no test pins the multiples and no source is cited.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SYSTEM_BY_NUMBER
constants.decides: How a space-group number maps to its crystal system (reduce.py:127).
constants.evidence: International Tables A's standard division of the 230 groups by number.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SYSTEM_BY_SYM_OPS
constants.decides: How a holohedral lattice group's rotation count maps to its crystal system (reduce.py:134).
constants.evidence: Physics: the seven holohedries -1, 2/m, mmm, 4/mmm, -3m, 6/mmm and m-3m have the rotation counts listed, and a lattice group is always holohedral.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SETTING_STEPS
constants.decides: How many Gauss steps a monoclinic re-set may take before it is declared stuck (reduce.py:477).
constants.evidence: A termination guard: each step at least halves |a.c| or shortens a vector, so 200 steps exceed double precision's range on any finite metric; tests/test_indexing_reduce.py::test_a_metric_that_is_no_lattice_has_no_setting covers the refusal path.
constants.question: No test reaches the cap itself: is the halving argument enough for tier 1?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SETTING_TIE
constants.decides: Below what relative size a.c or a^2 - c^2 is rounding rather than a choice in the monoclinic re-set (reduce.py:483).
constants.evidence: A numerical floor four orders above double rounding; tests/test_indexing_reduce.py::test_rounding_is_not_a_setting_to_re_set holds that rounding-level ties are not re-set.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._FACE_AXES
constants.decides: Which two axes each centred face spans, by letter (reduce.py:587).
constants.evidence: Definition: the A face spans b and c, the B face a and c.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.CELL_PINV_RCOND
constants.decides: The relative cut equal_reduced hands the pseudo-inverse of the summed covariance (reduce.py:630).
constants.evidence: numpy's own pinv default, a numerical floor; tests/test_indexing_reduce_boundaries.py:247-269 holds that the PSD pseudo-inverse is taken at it and a rounding eigenvalue cannot make chi-squared negative.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.SELLING_GATE_SIGMAS
constants.decides: How many Selling-scalar esds wide the gate is inside which the boundary-free test looks for b's other descriptions (reduce.py:747).
constants.measured_on: bethanechol (two dedup calls of 1 906 and 16 198 candidates)
constants.evidence: The root inherits CELL_EQUALITY_CHI2's tier; the 1.25 factor is rietx's own, and the groups were the same at 1.1, 1.25 and 2 times on bethanechol only. A gate and selector: the chi-squared on the image decides.
constants.question: Cauchy-Schwarz gives sufficiency at 1.0 to first order (reduce.py:741-744): is the factor answer-invariant if a test shows it?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce.SELLING_GATE_RELATIVE
constants.decides: The same gate for a pair without covariances, as a fraction of the larger metric trace (reduce.py:752).
constants.evidence: rietx's own: ten times CELL_EQUALITY_RELATIVE, a gate whose verdict the componentwise rule on the image decides; no test pins it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SELLING_DEPTH
constants.decides: How many reduction boundaries the cross-boundary equality crosses on each side (reduce.py:757).
constants.evidence: rietx's own: one step each side joined 604 of 608 split pairs and two steps on one side joined the other four; one family. A shallower depth splits one lattice into two candidates.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SELLING_PAIRS
constants.decides: Which vector pairs give Selling's six scalars (reduce.py:761).
constants.evidence: Definition: s1..s6 = b.c, a.c, a.b, a.d, b.d, c.d with d = -(a + b + c) (Andrews, Bernstein & Sauter 2019, A75, 115, section 2).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SELLING_START
constants.decides: The four starting vectors a, b, c and d = -(a + b + c) of a Selling reduction (reduce.py:764).
constants.evidence: Definition of Selling's superbase (Andrews, Bernstein & Sauter 2019, section 2).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._SELLING_STEPS
constants.decides: How many Selling steps a reduction may take before the pair keeps the answer of the vectors as given (reduce.py:768).
constants.evidence: A termination guard: each Selling step strictly lowers the sum of the four vectors' squared lengths, so a finite lattice reduces in far fewer steps; no test reaches the limit.
constants.question: Should a synthetic case reach the cap before the row is recorded?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._AF_ROW
constants.decides: Which G* row each A..F slot reads (reduce.py:897).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._AF_COL
constants.decides: Which G* column each A..F slot reads (reduce.py:898).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: the same definition of A..F as _AF_ROW.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.reduce._AF_TWO
constants.decides: The factor 2 on the off-diagonal A..F slots (reduce.py:899).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: D, E and F carry 2G*ij by definition.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.screen.SCREEN_WINDOW_LINES
constants.decides: The lines of de Wolff's window the capping count takes predicted positions up to (screen.py:96).
constants.evidence: Already tier 2 (_audit.py:2540): de Wolff (1968, J. Appl. Cryst. 1, 108)'s twenty, the window M20 is defined on, held as its own literal so a retune of fom.FOM_N cannot move it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.screen._LN2
constants.decides: ln 2 in the pseudo-Voigt profile (screen.py:97).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic, already tier 1 (_audit.py:2546).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.screen._LATTICE_POINTS
constants.decides: Lattice points per conventional cell for each centring letter, dividing a cell's volume to its primitive volume (screen.py:512).
constants.evidence: Physics: P 1, A/B/C/I 2, F 4, R 3 (hexagonal setting), the Bravais centring multiplicities.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.MAX_ITERATIONS
constants.decides: How many Table 1 step (iv) iterations an SVD call takes before giving up (svd.py:201).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003), J. Appl. Cryst. 36, 86-95: N_T1 = 20, the engine's published default; the corpus converges in 3-9 (svd.py:197-200).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.NC_NO_LO
constants.decides: The lower N_c/N_o ratio, which rietx reads as the upper end of the volume window V up to N_o/(3 kappa) (svd.py:206, volume_window at :641).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) Table 1 step (ii), the published value; rietx uses it as a volume window rather than a per-trial abort (svd.py:58-69), and that window held the true volume on all nine corpus datasets.
constants.question: The action changed (a precomputed window, not Coelho's per-trial abort): does the row need a tier-3 action entry beside the tier-2 value?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.NC_NO_HI
constants.decides: The upper N_c/N_o ratio, which bounds the volume window at 4 N_o/kappa (svd.py:206).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) Table 1 step (ii); tests/test_indexing_engines.py:2326-2340 holds that N_c counts distinct lines, the reading under which the certified LaB6 cell passes.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.VOLUME_LADDER_RATIO
constants.decides: The factor the SVD engine's volume ladder grows by per rung (svd.py:208, :866).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) eq. (3), nu_1 = 1.1, as the module cites it (svd.py:66, :207).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.CONTROL
constants.decides: How many random starts (N1) and perturbation rounds (N2) the SVD engine spends per volume rung in each crystal system (svd.py:213).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) Table 3, the engine's published control values (svd.py:209-212); tests/test_indexing_priors.py reads it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.WEIGHT_EXPONENT
constants.decides: The exponent m of Coelho's weighting W = d_o^m |d2theta| I_o, which decides which assignment the SVD iteration converges to (svd.py:237).
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) randomises m (over 0-4 in section 2.2, 0-6 in section 3.1); rietx fixes it at 4, measured to help NAC and hurt LaB6 at large perturbation. The value is inside the paper's range, the fixed choice is rietx's own.
constants.question: Is a fixed m = 4, inside a range Coelho randomises over, a tier-2 choice or rietx's own?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.TRIM_RETRY
constants.decides: How many lines at most are dropped when an SVD search that found nothing is retried (svd.py:242, :707).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: rietx's own: it rescues qarr corundum (0 to 3293 convergences in 4000 starts) and costs zircon, zincite and bethanechol F, so it runs only after silence (svd.py:86-97).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.MAX_BOX_INDEX
constants.decides: Above which |h| the SVD engine abandons a trial metric rather than enumerate its box (svd.py:247, _predicted at :298).
constants.evidence: A crash guard of rietx's own; hmax = floor(a sqrt(Q_max)) + 1, so a trial with a longest axis above about 40 d_min returns no lines and dies. No test reaches it, and nothing reports a cell lost to it.
constants.question: Can it drop a real long-axis cell (a above 40 d_min, a 40 Angstrom axis at d_min = 1 Angstrom), and should that be reported as a search bound?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.KAPPA_PROBES
constants.decides: How many random starts the kappa probe takes its median over, which places the SVD volume window (svd.py:251, :629).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: rietx's own: the comment says 24 moves the window's endpoints by under one per cent, without naming the data; the window held the truth on all nine corpus datasets.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.KAPPA_VOLUME
constants.decides: The reference volume the kappa probe scales its random cells to (svd.py:251, :631).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: rietx's own; kappa = N_c/V is volume-independent only to first order, and no test shows the window unmoved by the reference volume.
constants.question: Is it answer-invariant if a test shows the window does not move between reference volumes?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.ANGLE_LO
constants.decides: The lower end of the angle range random triclinic and monoclinic SVD starts are drawn from (svd.py:254, :578).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Coelho (2003) section 3 used 90-130 degrees to generate test lattices, not starts, so the printed value is the source and the use is rietx's own (generality.md: a printed value does not move a row to tier 2).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.ANGLE_HI
constants.decides: The upper end of the angle range random triclinic and monoclinic SVD starts are drawn from (svd.py:254).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: Same as ANGLE_LO: Coelho (2003) section 3's test-lattice range used for starts.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.IMPURITY_CUT_DEG
constants.decides: How far (degrees 2theta) an observed line may sit from its nearest calculated line in the last SVD pass before it is left unindexed (svd.py:260, :516).
constants.measured_on: WP-1040 corpus: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (zincite, zircon, corundum), GSAS-II fluorapatite, bethanechol published sets (five unrelated families)
constants.evidence: The last-pass rule is Coelho (2003) section 2.4 (svd.py:76-84, measured on zincite, zircon and fluorapatite); the comment does not say 0.05 degrees is his printed value.
constants.question: Is 0.05 degrees Coelho's own number (tier 2) or rietx's?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.svd.ZERO_ERROR_LIMIT_DEG
constants.decides: How large a zero error (degrees 2theta) an SVD pass may carry forward; larger is clipped (svd.py:271, :501).
constants.measured_on: LaB6 SRM 660c, qarr corundum, bethanechol A sets (svd.py:266-270)
constants.evidence: rietx's own: twice the 0.05 degrees Coelho (2003) says the strategy tolerates, and measured not to bind on SRM 660c (+0.033) or corundum (-0.067).

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.BASE_INDEX_MAX
constants.decides: The largest index a trial-and-error base line may be given, which decides which cells the engine can find (trial_error.py:82).
constants.measured_on: tests/indexing_gallery.py and tests/test_acceptance_indexing.py families: NIST SRM 660c LaB6, APS 11-BM NAC, IUCr CPD QPA round robin (corundum, zincite, zircon), GSAS-II fluorapatite tutorial list, bethanechol published sets
constants.evidence: rietx's own: a cell needing a higher index on a low-angle line is reported by INDEX_DOMINANT_ZONE naming the bound (tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1781-1800). No TREOR or ITO default is cited in the repo.
constants.question: Does TREOR90's or N-TREOR09's published base-line index limit match 2, which would make it tier 2?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.DOMINANT_ZONE_PROBE_LADDER
constants.decides: Which index ceilings the dominant-zone probe tries after a silent search, which decides whether INDEX_DOMINANT_ZONE is emitted (trial_error.py:89).
constants.measured_on: a synthetic tetragonal cell with c = 26 Angstrom (trial_error.py:84-88)
constants.evidence: rietx's own; the probe returns only a diagnostic, never a candidate. tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1781-1800 holds its first rung above BASE_INDEX_MAX.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.DOMINANT_ZONE_PROBE_SECONDS
constants.decides: How long one rung of the dominant-zone probe may run, which decides whether its diagnostic can appear (trial_error.py:104).
constants.measured_on: the synthetic construction of trial_error.py:84-88 (4.3 s serially)
constants.evidence: rietx's own runaway guard on a diagnostic, raised from 10 s in WP-1026 after a race under -n auto; tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1783-1791 reads it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.DOMINANT_ZONE_MAX_DOF
constants.decides: Above how many metric degrees of freedom the dominant-zone probe is skipped (trial_error.py:110).
constants.evidence: rietx's own cost bound; a dominant zone in an orthorhombic or lower cell goes undiagnosed, and no test covers that case.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.BASE_POOL_MIN
constants.decides: How many low-angle lines the trial-and-error base combinations are drawn from, which decides whether cross terms can be determined (trial_error.py:125).
constants.measured_on: a monoclinic cell (8.875, 16.408, 7.137, beta 93.84) in tests/test_indexing_engines.py:1223-1250
constants.evidence: rietx's own: a pool of six cannot determine E for that cell; the test asserts the pool is at least 8. One case, not three families.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.MAX_ASSIGN_PER_BASE
constants.decides: How many assignments are enumerated per base set before the index table is shrunk and the search reported incomplete (trial_error.py:130).
constants.evidence: A cost cap of rietx's own, reported as search_complete = False; same shape as MAX_GRID_BYTES (approved tier 3, 2026-10-31). No test reaches it.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.trial_error.SOLVE_CHUNK
constants.decides: How many rows one batched np.linalg.solve call takes (trial_error.py:133).
constants.evidence: Memory only: each row's n-by-n solve is independent of the batch it rides in, so the chunk size changes peak memory and never a solution.
constants.question: The rule asks for an invariance test: should one be built?

constants.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.ABSENT_SIGMA
constants.decides: How many propagated σ a predicted reflection's net intensity must reach to count as present, feeding the absent count, the extinction screen and validation (workflow.py:106).
constants.measured_on: qarr corundum (R-3c), magnetite (Fd-3m), zincite; NIST SRM 660c (Pm-3m, no extinctions) as the control
constants.evidence: rietx's own 3σ, matched to MATCH_SIGMA so one number means one thing; its failure mode on a correct cell is stated (a space-group extinction or an unreached high-angle line reads absent), and the 2θ of every flagged reflection travels with the count. Three qarr materials and the NIST control, two families by laboratory.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.VALIDATION_METRIC_REL
constants.decides: The relative metric error whose displacement the validation fit's windows must capture, setting the capture slack from the pattern's top angle (workflow.py:115).
constants.measured_on: the separation table's canonical 1 % wrong metric (tests/test_indexing_consensus.py)
constants.evidence: rietx's own assumed tolerance, stated as one: 1 % is the canonical wrong metric the separation table grades, so a wrong metric reads as displaced intensity rather than absent.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.VALIDATION_SLACK_BOUNDS_DEG
constants.decides: The floor and cap (0.3°, 6.0°) on the validation fit's derived capture slack (workflow.py:123).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, argued (the floor keeps a short-range synchrotron validation from tail-only windows, the cap keeps tan θ finite near 180°) and not measured.

constants.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.ABSENT_WINDOW_FWHM
constants.decides: The half-width, in predicted FWHM, of the window integrated to decide whether a predicted reflection is present (workflow.py:149).
constants.evidence: rietx's own, argued (a wider window on a dense supercell collects a neighbour's tail and reports a phantom as present) and not measured.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_POSITION_ESD_MAX_DEG
constants.decides: The position esd past which a fitted line is flagged position_unmeasured and leaves PeakList.usable().
constants.measured_on: 1 165 usable lines of 17 bundled lab patterns; FAP.XRA (GSAS tutorial)
constants.evidence: The bar is the axis: 2θ spans at most 180°, so an esd of 180° admits every angle and the line locates nothing (schemas/indexing.py:237-264); measured, the next-worst esd is 0.868°, 207× inside, and the one line it drops moved FAP's cell 1 376 ppm (WP-1442). Unanimity: none found who would match on a line of unbounded position.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_NO_INTENSITY_SIGMA
constants.decides: The I/σ_I under which a fitted component is flagged no_intensity and leaves PeakList.usable().
constants.measured_on: the 16 IUCr CPD round-robin lab patterns (one diffractometer, one family); FAP.XRA (GSAS tutorial); a forward-modelled silicon synthetic
constants.evidence: Measured: 2σ dropped eight real fluorapatite lines (I/σ_I 1.2-1.9), 1σ drops 6 of 798 usable round-robin lines and cleared the synthetic silicon's flank junk (schemas/indexing.py:266-282). Two real families plus a synthetic, under three. Unanimity: none found who would drive a search with a line at I < 1σ; the crystallographer's 2σ(I) convention dissents only in the stricter direction.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_FDR_Q
constants.decides: The false-discovery rate a picked list is held to; a component failing it is flagged weak_line, kept usable and out of the set the search is driven by.
constants.measured_on: the 16 IUCr CPD round-robin lab patterns (one diffractometer, one family); #728's steep-background synthetic silicon; F2's synthetic
constants.evidence: The statistic and rule are Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) over Detection.n_trials, tier 2, with astronomy's source-detection use cited (Miller et al. 2001; Hopkins et al. 2002); the rate 0.01 is the one F2's design names (schemas/indexing.py:284-314). Over the round robin it flags 13 of 789 usable components; one real family plus synthetics.
constants.question: Do the cited astronomy papers fix q = 0.01 by default, which would lift the threshold to tier 2?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_MIN_HEIGHT_SIGMA
constants.decides: The net height in channel σ a detection candidate must reach to be offered to the group fit.
constants.measured_on: KD1-2_5_NaCoO2 (tag guillemot-study), one lab pattern, for the σ-normalised form
constants.evidence: The σ-normalised form was measured against the prototype's relative prominence on one pattern; the value 5 is said to match the pattern-diagnostics census (schemas/indexing.py:316-326), which is rietx's own. No citation.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_MIN_PROMINENCE_SIGMA
constants.decides: The topographic prominence in local σ a detection candidate must reach.
constants.evidence: Argued lower than the height floor because a shoulder has small prominence by construction (schemas/indexing.py:328-331); no measurement or citation.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_SHOULDER_MIN_SIGMA
constants.decides: The significance a curvature (shoulder) seed must reach in the second-derivative filter's propagated noise.
constants.evidence: Multiple-comparison arithmetic over several hundred trials gives about one false shoulder per pattern at 3σ and about 1e-4 at 5σ (schemas/indexing.py:333-341); the target rate is rietx's, and the measurement is one synthetic.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_DETECT_SEPARATION_FWHM_FRAC
constants.decides: The closest two detections may sit, as a fraction of the narrowest predicted FWHM.
constants.evidence: Argued: smaller than the Pawley overlap fraction 0.5 so a 0.3-FWHM shoulder is offered and the ΔBIC test decides (schemas/indexing.py:343-348); no measurement.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_ALIAS_TOL_FWHM_FRAC
constants.decides: How close, in FWHM, a candidate must sit to a stronger line's Bragg-predicted Kα2 position to be dropped as its alias.
constants.evidence: Measured on one synthetic (one spurious line per resolved doublet without the filter); the 0.3 itself is not measured (schemas/indexing.py:350-361). The drop is reported as PEAK_KALPHA2_ALIAS.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_ALIAS_RATIO_RANGE
constants.decides: The observed height ratio, in multiples of the emission line's weight, inside which a Kα2-position candidate is accepted as an alias and dropped.
constants.evidence: Argued wide because partial overlap inflates the apparent Kα2 height (schemas/indexing.py:363-369); a genuine line at that position is indistinguishable in one pattern, so the drop is reported (PEAK_KALPHA2_ALIAS). Unanimity: a refiner who knows a second phase is present would keep such a line, so the action is reported rather than silent, and the range is unmeasured.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_WIDTH_CENSUS_N
constants.decides: How many of the most prominent detections the width census takes its median over, which sets the width scale for every seed and window.
constants.evidence: Measured on one pattern: the all-detections median read 0.071° against real 0.389° lines, the top-12 median recovers 0.389° (schemas/indexing.py:371-376). Under three families.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_POSITION_BOUND_FWHM
constants.decides: The half-width, in seed FWHM, of each component's position bound; a component that ends on it is flagged position_at_bound.
constants.measured_on: the 16 IUCr CPD round-robin lab patterns (one diffractometer, one family) (WP-2055)
constants.evidence: Argued as the analogue of VALIDITY_RADIUS_FWHM = 0.4; on the round robin 8 of 24 usable components on this bound were low-angle tail shoulders and freeing it moved seven further from any lattice line (schemas/indexing.py:378-390). The tree's docs/wp/2120 (WP-2120, open PR #1579) takes position_at_bound together with axial_tail as its subject, so its outcome may change what this bound's flag does.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_WIDTH_BOUND_FACTORS
constants.decides: The bounds on each fitted Gaussian and Lorentzian width as multiples of the seed width; a fit on the upper bound is flagged width_capped and leaves PeakList.usable().
constants.evidence: The lower 1e-4 is a positivity floor (tier 1 on its own, schemas/indexing.py:392-399); the upper 5 decides width_capped, an unusable flag (schemas/indexing.py:846-849, pick.py:384-385), and has no measurement or citation.
constants.question: Split the tuple's tiers (lower 1, upper 3) in the table?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_WINDOW_FWHM_MULT
constants.decides: The half-width of a group's fitting window, in seed FWHM beyond the outermost seed.
constants.evidence: Argued: a wider window buys baseline error against a frozen background, a narrower one costs Lorentzian precision (schemas/indexing.py:401-409); no measurement.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_WIDTH_SCALE_BOUNDS
constants.decides: The clamp on the global broadening factor fitted from the width census, which sets every seed width and window.
constants.evidence: Argued as a guard against a pathological census (schemas/indexing.py:411-416; peaks.py:452); no test shows an ordinary pattern stays inside it or names the case that reaches it.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_MAX_RESEED_PASSES
constants.decides: How many explicit re-seed passes may add a component to a group whose residual demands one.
constants.evidence: The frozen-per-stage argument decides why passes are separate, not why two (schemas/indexing.py:418-422); a third pass could add a component, so the cap moves the list and is not answer-invariant.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_KEEP_COMPONENT_MIN_DELTA_BIC
constants.decides: The ΔBIC an added component must clear to be kept in a group fit.
constants.evidence: Kass & Raftery (1995): 6 is the edge of the strong band, cited in schemas/indexing.py:424-428; the statistic is report.layer2.delta_bic.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_ASYMMETRY_MIN_SIGMA
constants.decides: The |t| of the residual's odd-cubic projection above which a peak is flagged asymmetric beyond the model; the flag does not leave usable().
constants.evidence: The odd-cubic direction is argued from a free position absorbing the first odd moment (schemas/indexing.py:430-434); the value 4 is neither measured nor cited, and the flag only reports.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_MIN_USABLE_LINES
constants.decides: The usable-line count below which the classical figures of merit are not computed and the fom_panel_reduced caveat caps confidence at medium; it never stops a search.
constants.evidence: de Wolff (1968) defines M₂₀ on the first twenty lines and Smith (1977) quotes the envelope at N = 20 (schemas/indexing.py:436-455); the engines' defaults in docs/practice.md agree (DICVOL card 2 N = 20, TREOR USE ≤ 20). Smith & Snyder recommend N = 30 for F_N, and scoring F_N at 20 is rietx's choice, said in the comment.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.METRIC_DOF
constants.decides: The number of free metric coefficients per crystal system, the denominator of lines per degree of freedom.
constants.evidence: Physics: the independent entries of A..F in Q(hkl) per system (schemas/indexing.py:457-466), used by tests/test_indexing_quality.py and three other test modules.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.MIN_LINES_PER_DOF
constants.decides: The usable lines per metric degree of freedom below which a crystal system is not searched, and below which in every system index_pattern abstains before any engine runs (workflow.py:962-976).
constants.measured_on: fluorite, IUCr round robin (18 lines, the case that motivated separating it from PEAK_MIN_USABLE_LINES)
constants.evidence: Argued as the smallest ratio at which a wrong cell is unlikely to match every line by accident (schemas/indexing.py:468-476); no measurement of the ratio and no citation. This is a gate that refuses rather than reports, which the WP asks about.
constants.question: Shown 4 lines per DOF, would every competent refiner decline to search that system, or would a DICVOL user run it and read the figures of merit?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.MAX_RELATIVE_SIGMA_Q
constants.decides: The median σ(Q)/Q above which index_pattern abstains on a fitted list before any engine runs; position-only lists are exempt (quality.py:486).
constants.measured_on: the ten published bethanechol peak sets (Bergmann et al. 2004), as the case the exemption was made for
constants.evidence: The bar has no citation or measurement (schemas/indexing.py:478-481). The rule 'an assumed precision may never refuse to index' (indexing/CLAUDE.md:319) holds in the tree: the abstention reads only source == 'fitted' (quality.py:486), after all ten bethanechol sets failed at their assumed σ (4.4e-3 on the synchrotron set, quality.py:407-410). On measured σ it still refuses, and the engines' published practice dissents: DICVOL and ITO search with a fixed 0.03° or 0.06° window whatever the precision (docs/practice.md:283-285); and since Q ∝ 1/a², a 0.1 % lattice difference is a 0.2 % Q difference, twice this bar per line, so the comment's 'indistinguishable' overstates it.
constants.question: Demote the refusal on measured σ to the PEAK_POSITION_PRECISION report (diagnostics.py:634-640) and run the search, since a named dissenter (DICVOL/ITO practice) exists?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_MAX_M
constants.decides: The largest harmonic order a reflection pair may have in the shift screen.
constants.evidence: m·sin θ ≤ 1 confines high-order pairs to low angle (arithmetic), but the cut at 8 is argued, not measured (schemas/indexing.py:497-505).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_WINDOW_DEG
constants.decides: The implied shift beyond which a candidate triple is not admitted as a reflection pair.
constants.evidence: Dong (1999) §3's own window, used there to find 11 pairs on a pattern carrying −0.182° (schemas/indexing.py:507-511).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_CLUSTER_HALF_WIDTH_DEG
constants.decides: The half-width of the window the concentration statistic slides over the implied shifts.
constants.measured_on: the WP-1038 corpus of fitted lists: IUCr round robin, SRM 660c LaB6, GSAS tutorial FAP/NAC
constants.evidence: Measured: real clusters have σ 0.0033-0.0071° across the corpus, so 0.010 holds one whole (schemas/indexing.py:513-516).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_NULL_REPLICATES
constants.decides: The number of structureless replicates the pair concentration is tested against, which sets the empirical p floor at 1/201.
constants.evidence: 1/201 is below the 0.01 bar (arithmetic, schemas/indexing.py:518-520), but PAIR_MAX_P's own comment records a verdict that changed with the rng sequence, so the replicate count is a numerical setting with no test bounding its effect on the verdict.
constants.question: Would a test that the verdicts on the corpus are stable across seeds at 200 replicates make this tier 1?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_MIN_Z
constants.decides: The concentration z below which the pair method declines to report a shift.
constants.measured_on: 3 600 null replicates over 18 line lists; seven real fitted lists of the WP-1038 corpus (round robin, SRM 660c, GSAS tutorial)
constants.evidence: Measured: z ≥ 3.0 fires on 0.83 % of nulls and z ≥ 3.5 on one replicate, while every real fitted list scores z ≥ 4.2 (schemas/indexing.py:522-527).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_MAX_P
constants.decides: The empirical p a concentration must also clear to report a shift, and the only bar used to refute a losing template.
constants.evidence: A conventional 0.01 chosen for small-count robustness after sin_2theta escaped refutation on SRM 660c on one rng draw (schemas/indexing.py:529-537); no citation.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_MIN_CLUSTERED
constants.decides: The number of pairs that must agree before a shift amplitude is quoted.
constants.evidence: Dong (1999) §3 asks for at least three reflection pairs with close zero shifts (schemas/indexing.py:539-541).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PAIR_REFUTE_K_FRACTION
constants.decides: How far below the winner's concentration a template must fall, together with an insignificant z, to be reported refuted.
constants.measured_on: the WP-1038 corpus; zircon from the IUCr round robin
constants.evidence: Measured: sin_2theta sits at 0.30-0.50 of the winner wherever a shift exists, and zircon's constant at 7 against cos_theta's 8 is the one-pair case it stops (schemas/indexing.py:543-551).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.SHIFT_ALLOWANCE_K_ESD
constants.decides: The standard errors of the fitted shift amplitude added as headroom to the matching window.
constants.measured_on: corundum SRM 676a (IUCr round robin) and SRM 660c LaB6, two certified families (WP-1038)
constants.evidence: Swept against certified answers: corundum keeps R to 0.070° and flips at 0.0767°, SRM 660c flips at 0.0532° and at 0.060° returns a cell 293 000 ppm off at high confidence; 3 standard errors put corundum at 0.0681° (schemas/indexing.py:553-577). Two families, under three, and validated against certificates.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.SMITH_VOLUME_C1
constants.decides: The published constant 0.6 of Smith's (1977) volume envelope V ≈ 0.6·d_N³/(1/N − 0.0052), which sets the volume ceiling the data support.
constants.evidence: Smith (1977), kept as the two published constants because the formula is used at other N (schemas/indexing.py:579-581). Under the 2026-11-05 ruling a printed value is the row's source and does not by itself test the number, so the citation is the evidence.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.SMITH_VOLUME_C2
constants.decides: The published constant 0.0052 of Smith's (1977) volume envelope V ≈ 0.6·d_N³/(1/N − 0.0052), which sets the volume ceiling the data support.
constants.evidence: Smith (1977), kept as the two published constants because the formula is used at other N (schemas/indexing.py:579-581). Under the 2026-11-05 ruling a printed value is the row's source and does not by itself test the number, so the citation is the evidence.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.INDEX_MIN_INDEXED_FRACTION
constants.decides: The share of the usable lines' intensity a candidate must index (else the refuting indexed_fraction_low) and of their count (else the capping indexed_lines_low) before it can grade high.
constants.measured_on: SRM 660c LaB6 with injected weak and strong impurity lines (WP-1969, issue #933)
constants.evidence: McMaille's published scoring tolerates impurities holding under 10-15 % of the total intensity (Le Bail 2004, docs/practice.md § Which lines an indexing search is given), and 0.9 explained sits inside that range; measured, SRM 660c explains 0.93-1.00 with up to six weak impurity lines and 0.73-0.74 with six strong ones (schemas/indexing.py:583-625). The caveat vocabulary INDEX_REFUTING_CAVEATS (schemas/indexing.py:703-706, no row: a frozenset of strings the walk drops) refutes on geometric_ambiguity, fom_panel_disagrees, indexed_fraction_low, volume_unphysical, validation_failed and supercell_refuted, and caps on engines_disagree, fom_panel_reduced, not_validated, predicted_but_absent (capping since 1.12), indexed_lines_low, search_incomplete, shift_allowance_assumed and bravais_ambiguous.
constants.question: Is McMaille's impurity tolerance a published default this gate may rest on (tier 2), or a scoring weight unlike a grade gate (tier 3)? And in the caveat vocabulary, should geometric_ambiguity written for a candidate the ambiguity search never reached (consensus.py:627-632, WP-1986) and fom_panel_disagrees refute, or cap?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_ASSUMED_ESD_DEG
constants.decides: The σ(2θ) PeakList.from_positions gives a bare position list by default, which sets every line's σ(Q) and so the ±kσ matching windows the engines and figures of merit read.
constants.measured_on: the ten published bethanechol peak sets (Bergmann et al. 2004); hl2's bare list
constants.evidence: Called a typical well-aligned lab precision with no measurement (schemas/indexing.py:708-714); every such line carries sigma_assumed. At 3σ the window is 0.06° 2θ, between DICVOL's 0.03° default and ITO's TOLG 0.06° (docs/practice.md:283-285), which may make the value tier 2 on the engines' defaults. Per WP-2013's follow-up, index_pattern emits no PEAK_SIGMA_ASSUMED for such a list; only peak_diagnostics does.
constants.question: Tier 2 on the engines' windows (the 3σ window inside DICVOL-ITO's range), or tier 3? And should index_pattern emit PEAK_SIGMA_ASSUMED for a from_positions list?

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_AXIAL_TAIL_MAX_FWHM
constants.decides: The distance in fitted FWHM within which a weak component on the aberration's side of a stronger group-mate is flagged axial_tail; the flag does not leave usable().
constants.measured_on: the SRM 660c LaB6 census (WP-1028, WP-1043); six real lab patterns for the unverified hits
constants.evidence: 3.5 spans the farthest measured SRM 660c tail at 2.99 FWHM, and the one-sided sign flip at 90° is a physics signature (schemas/indexing.py:815-829). The tree's docs/wp/2120 (WP-2120, open PR #1579) takes axial_tail together with position_at_bound as its subject.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_REFUTED_SIGMA
constants.decides: The standard deviations above χ²_red = 1 at which a group fit is refuted, so a component added to it is flagged not_separable and leaves usable().
constants.measured_on: the bundled IUCr round-robin corundum pattern (Cu Kα, lab Bragg-Brentano)
constants.evidence: The statistic is arithmetic (σ(χ²_red) = √(2/ν), tier 1); the 3σ is the package's convention, the same as fom.MATCH_SIGMA, with no citation in the tree (schemas/indexing.py:874-911). Measured on one family, where satellites at χ²_red 17.4 and 4.6 stopped both engines and removing them indexed the certified cell; the comment states the failure mode (a genuine weak neighbour of a badly fitted group is demoted).

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_SATELLITE_NEAR_FWHM
constants.decides: The distance in fitted FWHM within which a re-seeded weak component counts as inside a neighbour's profile, one of the three conditions of not_separable.
constants.evidence: No measurement for this distance (schemas/indexing.py:913-916); PEAK_AXIAL_TAIL_MAX_FWHM's comment records that widening it reached four of six tails, so the census bears on it only indirectly.

constants.name: rietx.schemas.indexing.PEAK_SATELLITE_MAX_RATIO
constants.decides: The area ratio below which a component is a satellite of a group-mate, read by not_separable, the merge test, the axial-tail screen and the Kα2-residual flag.
constants.measured_on: the qarr lab patterns (IUCr round robin), one family
constants.evidence: Measured satellite ratios 0.08-0.14 on one family; 0.25 is set above them (schemas/indexing.py:918-920).

constants.name: rietx.solve.chemistry.OCCUPANCY_MAX_DENOMINATOR
constants.decides: The largest denominator a part occupancy is read as a fraction of in Composition.require (solve/chemistry.py:102).
constants.measured_on: not measured (three published part-occupied structures pending)
constants.evidence: Current tier 3, approved 2026-10-24 on the judgement ground (_audit.py:4303); tests/test_solve_chemistry.py::test_the_inventory_tolerance_scales_with_the_part_occupied_multiplicity.

constants.name: rietx.solve.chemistry._CELLS27
constants.decides: The 27 lattice translations around a minimum image for the clash term (solve/chemistry.py:364).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: the translations (-1, 0, 1) cubed, with (0, 0, 0) at index 13.

constants.name: rietx.solve.cluster._ISOMETRY_RTOL
constants.decides: When an integer matrix is an isometry of the cell in equivalences() (solve/cluster.py:79).
constants.evidence: Current tier 1 (_audit.py:4285): ten orders above rounding; test_the_normaliser_index_is_international_tables and test_a_metrically_special_cell_is_judged_at_the_isometry_tolerance (tests/test_solve_engine.py).

constants.name: rietx.solve.cluster._CELLS27
constants.decides: The 27 lattice translations around a minimum image in the cluster module (solve/cluster.py:80).
constants.evidence: Arithmetic: itertools.product((-1, 0, 1), repeat=3).

constants.name: rietx.solve.cost.NUISANCE_RCOND
constants.decides: Below what fraction of the largest eigenvalue of the equilibrated nuisance normal matrix a direction is dropped from the pseudo-inverse (solve/cost.py:136, :388).
constants.measured_on: APS 11-BM NAC and the two-phase fixture of tests/test_solve_cost.py
constants.evidence: A numerical floor on a unit-diagonal matrix; tests/test_solve_cost.py::test_chi2_does_not_depend_on_the_impurity_s_stored_scale holds chi-squared unmoved over eight decades of a nuisance column's scale, and :205-231 holds the cost to 1e-13 against an independent pinv at the same cut.

constants.name: rietx.solve.cost.NAMED_REFLECTIONS
constants.decides: How many reflections an ExtractionRefused message names before it counts the rest (solve/cost.py:142, _named at :208).
constants.evidence: A cap on what a refusal lists: _named appends 'and N more', so the message counts what lies outside it and the refusal does not depend on the number.
constants.question: No test asserts the 'and N more' count: should one be added for the tier-1 cap clause?

constants.name: rietx.solve.moves._TAU
constants.decides: The 2 pi in the structure-factor phase (solve/moves.py:103).
constants.evidence: Current tier 1 (_audit.py:4324): arithmetic, the phase of exp(2 pi i h.x).

constants.name: rietx.solve.tempering.REFRESH_EVERY
constants.decides: How many sweeps pass between full rebuilds of the running orbit sums in temper() (solve/tempering.py:73).
constants.measured_on: acridine-shaped synthetic case and APS 11-BM NAC
constants.evidence: Current tier 1 (_audit.py:4326): a numerical setting; tests/test_solve_engine.py::test_running_sums_stay_on_a_rebuild holds the drift under 1e-10 J at the cadence.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:peaks
defaults.decides: The peak list to index; with None the package picks one from data and instrument (pick_peaks) or raises (workflow.py:866-871).
defaults.evidence: The caller's input: supplying a list or a pattern is the caller's act, and the picker's own numbers are tiered at their rows in indexing/pick.py and indexing/peaks.py.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:data
defaults.decides: The powder pattern; supplying it turns whole-pattern validation on, and without it every candidate caps at medium with INDEX_NOT_VALIDATED (workflow.py:734-760).
defaults.evidence: The caller's input; the package chooses nothing at this seat, and what a missing pattern costs is reported (INDEX_NOT_VALIDATED).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:instrument
defaults.decides: The instrument the picker and validation read; required with data when peaks is None (workflow.py:866-871).
defaults.evidence: The caller's input; None with no peaks raises rather than assuming a wavelength.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:spec
defaults.decides: spec=None resolves to SearchSpec(), the search's whole control surface (workflow.py:870).
defaults.evidence: A delegation: every decision behind it is a SearchSpec field default, tiered at the seat rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec (17 rows here).
defaults.question: Is n/a acceptable for a None that only delegates to another seat, or should the row carry the lowest tier among SearchSpec's fields (3) (workflow.py:870)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:preset
defaults.decides: preset=None resolves to the quick preset, a 120 s whole-run ceiling covering search, probe and validation (workflow.py:871-881).
defaults.evidence: preset=None resolves to DEFAULT_SEARCH_PRESET = "quick" (engines.py:2347, workflow.py:873), a string the walk drops, which fills QUICK_TOTAL_BUDGET_SECONDS (120 s) into total_budget_seconds unless the caller declared one. Under DESIGN.md § Rules, 1 the preset is not a verdict: it stops the search and reports what it cut (INDEX_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED names truncated and unreached systems), so its answer is a second-kind ranking over the systems reached, justified as a default by the token clause, and a refiner indexing a low-symmetry organic who would let the search run (DICVOL04 to 3770 s, indexing/CLAUDE.md) is the named dissenter to treating the cut as first kind. Its budgets are tier 3 on four high-symmetry families (WP-1042), not answer-invariant.
defaults.question: Keep quick as the default on the token clause with its budgets at tier 3, and re-measure the ceiling on a low-symmetry family before approval (engines.py:2345)? Separately, #1374's share rule under a declared ceiling: cap each unit at min(budget_seconds, T_search / n_engines) so one unit cannot hold the whole ceiling, per engine or over the remaining units?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:engines
defaults.decides: engines=None runs every registered engine (dichotomy, svd, trial_error); high means every engine that ran found the lattice (workflow.py:892).
defaults.evidence: rietx's own design: engines that fail differently must agree before a lattice is corroborated (indexing/CLAUDE.md § The governing rule), and restricting the list narrows what the answer can say. Running all is the no-narrowing default; no established program runs several indexing engines by default in the repo's survey.
defaults.question: Is running every registered engine a first-kind default (nobody would narrow by default) and so tier 1, or rietx's own (3) because the set of engines decides the corroboration the gate reads (workflow.py:892)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:quality
defaults.decides: quality=None computes the data-quality report from the peaks (assess_peak_list), which sets the volume envelope, the measured shift and the supported systems (workflow.py:887-889).
defaults.evidence: A delegation: the report's own numbers (Smith's envelope, VOLUME_ENVELOPE_SLACK, the pair screen) are tiered at their rows; passing one in is the caller's act.
defaults.question: Is n/a acceptable here, as for spec (workflow.py:887)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:shift_from_pairs
defaults.decides: Whether the harmonic-pair screen (Dong 1999) measures a shift magnitude from the peak list alone, which then sizes the search window (workflow.py:741, :888).
defaults.evidence: The statistic is Dong (1999)'s; adopting it as the window by default is rietx's own (WP-1038), measured on NIST SRM 660c (a certified shift recovered from the list), qarr corundum (one shift from a multi-phase pattern) and 11-BM NAC (the published false-pair rule admits it at chance; the seeded null rejects it), three families. It sizes windows only and never moves a cell; the allowance is reported as INDEX_SHIFT_ALLOWANCE.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:validate
defaults.decides: Whether checked candidates get a whole-pattern validation fit when a pattern is supplied; it is what lets a candidate leave medium (workflow.py:742).
defaults.evidence: The validation fit is Pawley since WP-2011 (workflow.VALIDATION_MODE = "pawley", workflow.py:119, a string the walk cannot see; LeBailValidation.mode records it per candidate), tier 2 on docs/practice.md's survey: TOPAS defaults to Pawley (Technical Reference v5 §8) and its indexing GUI refines each selected solution by Pawley or Le Bail (docs/practice.md:557-570, 603-604). Without validation every candidate caps at medium with INDEX_NOT_VALIDATED; PAWLEY_OVERLAP_FWHM_FRAC (tier 3, _audit.py:2741) is also read by the peak picker (indexing/peaks.py:42, :308), so its opt-in-Pawley ground no longer holds on index_pattern's path.
defaults.question: Validation adds evidence and refuses nothing, but a batch screener who wants speed would turn it off; is that a dissent to the default or only to its cost, which the validation reserve bounds inside the ceiling (workflow.py:742)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:check_top
defaults.decides: check_top=None resolves to CONSENSUS_CHECK_TOP, three plus every promotable candidate (workflow.py:893).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.consensus.CONSENSUS_CHECK_TOP's proposed tier: a cap tested never to remove a promotable candidate (tests/test_indexing_consensus.py:518-529).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:two_theta_limits
defaults.decides: two_theta_limits=None uses the pattern's whole range for picking and validation (workflow.py:744).
defaults.evidence: Off by default: None narrows nothing, and a range is the caller's declared act; the package chooses nothing inside it.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:formula
defaults.decides: formula=None records no formula units on the candidates (workflow.py:745).
defaults.evidence: Already caller (_audit.py:5140): opt-in, a formula only records formula_units and moves no search, rank or grade (WP-2030).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:temperature
defaults.decides: The temperature at which Hofmann's (2002) volumes are read when a formula is supplied (workflow.py:745).
defaults.evidence: Used only once the formula switch is on, so tiered on its own: 298 K is the temperature Hofmann (2002) tabulates his volumes at (Table 2's caption and § 3, crystallography/atomic_volume.py:16-31, TABLE_TEMPERATURE). It moves the reported formula_units only.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:events
defaults.decides: events=None streams no progress events (workflow.py:746).
defaults.evidence: Off by default; an event sink is the caller's, and the stream (provisional cells, per-system consensus) moves nothing in the returned result.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:cancel
defaults.decides: cancel=None runs without a cancel token beyond the preset's deadline (workflow.py:746).
defaults.evidence: Off by default; a token is the caller's, and a cancelled run returns a complete result over what it reached.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:systems
defaults.decides: Searches all seven systems, in SYSTEM_ORDER (cubic, hexagonal, trigonal, tetragonal, orthorhombic, monoclinic, triclinic), the order a binding ceiling cuts from the end (engines.py:58, :360).
defaults.evidence: All seven is the no-narrowing choice; the order (cheapest metric first) is rietx's own (WP-1042) and decides, under quick, which systems are cut, reported by INDEX_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Measured on the high-symmetry corpus, where the truth's system finished first on every run.
defaults.question: Is the cheapest-first order an answer-deciding choice that needs a low-symmetry family under quick, as #1374's all-systems monoclinic rows suggest (engines.py:58)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:centrings
defaults.decides: centrings=None searches every Bravais centring each system admits (CENTRINGS, engines.py:67).
defaults.evidence: Physics: CENTRINGS lists the fourteen Bravais lattices in conventional settings (cubic P I F, trigonal P R, tetragonal P I, orthorhombic P C I F, monoclinic P C, hexagonal and triclinic P); a centred filter prunes rather than adds work.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:min_d_axis
defaults.decides: The default 2.0 Å lower bound on d(100) (DEFAULT_MIN_D_AXIS).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MIN_D_AXIS's proposed tier and question.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:max_d_axis
defaults.decides: The default 25 Å upper bound on a principal d-spacing (DEFAULT_MAX_D_AXIS).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MAX_D_AXIS's proposed tier.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:min_volume
defaults.decides: The default 15 Å³ volume floor (DEFAULT_MIN_VOLUME).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MIN_VOLUME's proposed tier and question.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:max_volume
defaults.decides: max_volume=None takes the per-system ceiling from the data-quality report, VOLUME_ENVELOPE_SLACK × Smith's envelope, else DEFAULT_VOLUME_CEILING (engines.py:1276, search_volume_ceiling).
defaults.evidence: Smith's envelope is the cited statistic; the slack and the fallback are rietx's own (VOLUME_ENVELOPE_SLACK, DEFAULT_VOLUME_CEILING). A declared ceiling is used verbatim and recorded in spec_notes.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:n_unindexed
defaults.decides: n_unindexed=None accepts with DEFAULT_N_UNINDEXED (2) on the first pass and retries under the inlier rule when no lattice has two engines' agreement (engines.py:366-370).
defaults.evidence: Follows DEFAULT_N_UNINDEXED and INLIER_FRACTION (tier 3); the retry after silence has precedent (Bergmann et al. 2004, DICVOL91's advice, docs/practice.md:730-731), and it is not the default for every run because it moves the pool Borda ranks (SRM 660c LaB6 rank 1 to 3).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:n_search_lines
defaults.decides: The default twenty driven lines (DEFAULT_SEARCH_LINES).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_SEARCH_LINES: the indexing engines' published defaults sit at twenty (docs/practice.md:681-713).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:k_sigma
defaults.decides: The default matching window of 3σ_eff (MATCH_SIGMA).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.fom.MATCH_SIGMA's proposed tier and question.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:shift_allowance_deg
defaults.decides: 0.0 declares no window, so the package sizes it: the pair screen's measured allowance, else the width allowance capped at DEFAULT_UNKNOWN_SHIFT_DEG (effective_shift_allowance).
defaults.evidence: The value itself declares nothing; what decides is the fallback chain, whose cap is tier 2 (the programs' 0.03-0.06° windows) and whose width rule is tier 3 (WIDTH_ALLOWANCE_FWHM), so the lower tier is proposed.
defaults.question: Should a delegating zero carry the lower tier of its fallback chain, or n/a with the tiers left on the constants (engines.py:382)?

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:shift_template
defaults.decides: shift_template=None moves no cell for a shift; a measured shift only sizes windows (engines.py:383).
defaults.evidence: Off by default: declaring a template (constant, cos θ, sin 2θ) is the caller's act, since the magnitude is knowable from the list and the cause is not (indexing/CLAUDE.md § The search window and the shift). The cost of the off default, a cell biased by roughly the shift, is reported (INDEX_SHIFT_ALLOWANCE, shift_allowance_assumed keeps high unreachable).

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:budget_seconds
defaults.decides: The default 30 s per (engine × system) unit (DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS).
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_BUDGET_SECONDS's proposed tier and #1374's question.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:total_budget_seconds
defaults.decides: total_budget_seconds=None lets the preset decide; under the default quick preset it becomes 120 s, and a declared value records preset custom (engines.py:395).
defaults.evidence: Follows QUICK_TOTAL_BUDGET_SECONDS (tier 3, not answer-invariant) through the preset seat; see rietx.indexing.workflow.index_pattern:preset for the preset's kind under DESIGN.md § Rules, 1.

defaults.name: rietx.indexing.engines.SearchSpec:max_candidates
defaults.decides: The default reported cap of twelve (DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES); the unit pool is five times it.
defaults.evidence: Follows rietx.indexing.engines.DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES's proposed tier and its question on WP-2112 (WP-1046 is where the cap moved to the reported layer).

defaults.decides: The seed of the stochastic svd engine, part of its answer and recorded in every result (engines.py:399).

defaults.question: Is a recorded fixed seed tier 1 as a reproducibility setting, or should a seed sweep on the corpus show the ranking is seed-insensitive first (engines.py:399)?

defaults.decides: No analogue prior cells by default (engines.py:408).
defaults.evidence: Off by default: a prior is the caller's declared knowledge; it steers and never gates, and the numbers used once it is on (priors.py constants) are tiered at their rows.

defaults.decides: No analogue prior space groups by default (engines.py:409).
defaults.evidence: Off by default, as prior_cells; INDEX_PRIOR_USED records what was supplied.
